COUNTRY:                           Federal Republic of Somalia (FGS)

NAME OF PROJECT          Somalia Recurrent Cost & Reform Financing (RCRF) Project - Phase III                                  

PROJECT ID                          P173731

Grant No.                            IDA-E3120

Assignment Title: Special Audit of Payroll Data Migration and Integrity in Somalia Federal Member States. Reference No: SO-MOF-564851-CS-CQS

Place of assignment:  Mogadishu and other Federal Member States of Somalia

Background

I. The Federal Government of Somalia, through the Ministry of Finance has received financing from the World Bank for the Somalia Recurrent Cost and Reform Financing Project that supports the FGS and eligible Federal Member States (FMS) in strengthening resource management systems, the intergovernmental fiscal relations, and service delivery in health and education. The project disburses financing against Performance-Based Conditions (PBCs), under which payment follows independently verified evidence that agreed reform milestones have been achieved, rather than against inputs alone. The objective of the audit is to provide reasonable assurance on payroll migration completeness, legitimacy of payroll entries, authorized payment execution, and resolution of material control weaknesses.

II. The Government intends to apply part of the proceeds in the Procurement of Consulting Special Audit of Payroll Data Migration and Integrity in Somalia Federal Member States

III. The Ministry of Finance now invites eligible firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.  

The short-listing criteria are as follows:

A. Core business and years in business: The firm must be a registered, audit or professional services firm, affiliated with an institute that is a full member of the International Federation of Accountants (IFAC) with a core business focus on financial and auditing. The firm must have been in operation for ten (10) years.

B. Relevant Experience: The firm should demonstrate experience in financial auditing, public financial management, HR, or governance, with successful execution of at least two (2) similar assignments. For each referenced assignment, provide evidence related to the assignment, including title, scope of work, client name, address, and contact details, duration, and contract value.

C. Technical and managerial capacity: The firm should demonstrate sufficient technical and managerial capacity to carry out the assignment.; and

D. The technical and managerial capability of the firm. (Provide  the structure of the organization, general qualifications, and the number of key staff, thier CVs and their qualifications.

IV. Terms of Reference:

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) can be found at the following website: www.mof.gov.so  or it can be forwarded to the applicant upon submission of the application to the address indicated below.

V. Selection Method:

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to section III, para 3.14, 3.16 & 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Projects Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, "Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers" July 2016, revised November 2017 revised August 2018, November 2020, 2023 and 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest and eligibility.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant Qualification Selection (CQS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations. Interested Consultants may obtain further information at the address below during office hours from 8:30 am to 3.30 pm Mogadishu time (Excluding public holidays).

Expressions of interest (EOI) should be delivered by e-mail below indicating “SO-MOF-564851-CS-CQS Procurement of Consulting Special Audit of Payroll Data Migration and Integrity in Somalia Federal Member States); on the email subject to the address below by  2nd  September 2026 at 12:00 Hours (Mogadishu Time)2026 at 12:00 Hours (Mogadishu Time)

data.notice_text:
REPUBLIC OF ZAMBIA

MINISTRY OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT AND RURAL DEVELOPMENT

REPUBLIC OF ZAMBIA

MINISTRY OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT AND RURAL DEVELOPMENT

ZAMBIA DEVOLUTION SUPPORT PROGRAMME (ZDSP)

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT

 

 

Assignment Title: Individual Consultant to Develop Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM) Standard Operating Procedures and Tools for Local Authorities

Project: Zambia Devolution Support Programme (ZDSP)

Assignment Duration: Eight (8) weeks

Reference No.: ZM-MLGRD-567788-CS-INDV

1. Background

The Government of the Republic of Zambia, through the Ministry of Local Government and Rural Development, is implementing the Zambia Devolution Support Programme (ZDSP) with support from the World Bank. The Programme seeks to strengthen local governance systems, support the decentralisation agenda and enhance service delivery at the local authority level.

Effective grievance management is an important element of accountable, transparent and citizen-responsive governance. Local Authorities are required to have functional mechanisms through which citizens, communities, project beneficiaries and other stakeholders can raise concerns, complaints, suggestions and feedback relating to service delivery, project implementation, environmental and social impacts and other governance matters.

Under the ZDSP, there is a need to establish a standardized and practical approach to grievance management across participating Local Authorities. The assignment will therefore support the development of Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM) Standard Operating Procedures and practical tools that can be adopted and applied by Local Authorities.

The Ministry of Local Government and Rural Development now invites eligible individual consultants to indicate their interest in providing the services described below.

2. Objective of the Assignment

The main objective of the assignment is to develop Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM) Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and supporting tools to guide Local Authorities in receiving, recording, assessing, investigating, resolving, monitoring and reporting grievances in a timely, transparent, accessible and accountable manner.

The specific objectives are to:

  • Review existing grievance management practices and systems within Local Authorities;
  • Develop GRM Standard Operating Procedures applicable across Local Authorities;
  • Establish clear grievance handling workflows, roles, responsibilities and escalation pathways;
  • Develop standardized GRM templates, forms, registers and reporting tools;
  • Ensure integration of relevant Environmental and Social requirements, including appropriate referral protocols for Sexual Exploitation and Abuse/Sexual Harassment (SEA/SH);
  • Strengthen accountability, transparency, inclusiveness and citizen participation; and
  • Provide practical guidance for monitoring, reporting and continuous improvement of grievance management systems.

3. Scope of Services

The selected Individual Consultant will be required to undertake, among others, the following tasks:

A. Review and Assessment

The Consultant will:

  • Review relevant national legislation, policies, regulations and guidelines relating to grievance management, public participation, local governance and related matters;
  • Review relevant ZDSP implementation frameworks and applicable World Bank Environmental and Social Framework requirements;
  • Assess existing grievance handling systems and practices within selected Local Authorities;
  • Identify strengths, gaps, challenges and opportunities for improving existing grievance management systems; and
  • Prepare an assessment report presenting the findings and recommendations.

B. Development of GRM Standard Operating Procedures

The Consultant will develop comprehensive GRM SOPs covering, among other areas:

  • Purpose, scope and guiding principles of the GRM;
  • Institutional arrangements and governance structures;
  • Roles and responsibilities of relevant actors at different levels;
  • Grievance intake and registration;
  • Classification and screening of grievances;
  • Investigation and assessment;
  • Resolution and response mechanisms;
  • Communication and feedback to complainants;
  • Case closure;
  • Appeals and escalation procedures;
  • Referral pathways for specialized and sensitive cases;
  • Confidentiality and appropriate data protection measures;
  • Accessibility for vulnerable groups and persons with disabilities;
  • Survivor-centred referral arrangements for SEA/SH-related cases;
  • Documentation and record management;
  • Monitoring, evaluation and reporting; and
  • Continuous improvement of GRM performance.

C. Development of Standardized GRM Tools

The Consultant shall develop practical, user-friendly and standardized GRM tools, including but not limited to:

  • Grievance Submission Form;
  • Complaint Intake Form;
  • Grievance Register;
  • Case Investigation Form;
  • Referral Form;
  • Grievance Resolution Form;
  • Appeal Form;
  • Case Closure Form;
  • Monthly GRM Reporting Template;
  • Quarterly GRM Reporting Template;
  • Grievance Tracking Dashboard Template;
  • Standard GRM Process Flow Charts;
  • Grievance Logbooks; and
  • Appropriate electronic/database templates for grievance tracking and reporting.

D. Stakeholder Consultations and Validation

The Consultant will undertake consultations with relevant stakeholders, including representatives of the Ministry, ZDSP Programme Management Unit, Local Authorities and other relevant stakeholders, as appropriate.

The Consultant will facilitate a validation process/workshop to present the draft GRM SOPs and tools, obtain stakeholder feedback and incorporate agreed comments and recommendations into the final deliverables.

4. Expected Deliverables

The Consultant will be expected to produce the following deliverables:

No.

Deliverable

Indicative Timeline

1

Inception Report, including methodology, work plan and assignment schedule

Week 1

2

Assessment Report, including findings from the review of existing GRM systems and stakeholder consultations

Weeks 2–3

3

Draft GRM SOPs and Standardized GRM Tools

Weeks 4–5

4

Validation Workshop/Consultation Report

Week 6

 

 

 

5

Final GRM SOPs and Standardized GRM Tools incorporating agreed comments

Week 7

6

Assignment Completion Report, including activities undertaken, outputs, lessons learned and recommendations

Week 8

All deliverables shall be submitted in editable electronic formats, as appropriate, and shall be of a standard suitable for adoption and implementation by Local Authorities.

5. Duration of the Assignment

The assignment is expected to be completed within eight (8) weeks from the date of contract signing.

6. Reporting and Supervision

The Individual Consultant will report to the Director – Physical Planning, Ministry of Local Government and Rural Development, with technical support from the ZDSP Programme Management Unit, including the Programme Coordinator and Environmental and Social Safeguards Specialists.

7. Required Qualifications and Experience

The Individual Consultant should possess the following minimum qualifications and experience:

  • An advanced university degree (Master's degree or equivalent) in Social Sciences, Public Administration, Law, Governance, Development Studies or another relevant discipline;
  • At least seven (7) years of relevant professional experience in grievance management, social safeguards, governance, accountability systems, stakeholder engagement or related fields;
  • Demonstrated experience in developing and/or operationalizing Grievance Redress Mechanisms and Standard Operating Procedures;
  • Demonstrated experience in developing practical institutional procedures, forms, registers, reporting templates and related operational tools;
  • Good knowledge and understanding of decentralisation and local government systems in Zambia;
  • Demonstrated experience in stakeholder consultation and facilitation;
  • Strong analytical, report-writing and communication skills;
  • Knowledge and experience in applying the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and relevant Environmental and Social Standards will be an advantage; and
  • Experience in developing GRM systems incorporating provisions for vulnerable groups, confidentiality and sensitive grievances, including SEA/SH referral pathways, will be an advantage.

8. Expression of Interest

The Ministry of Local Government and Rural Development now invites eligible individual consultants to indicate their interest in undertaking the assignment.

Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services. The Expression of Interest should include:

  1. A brief Expression of Interest/cover letter indicating the Consultant's interest in undertaking the assignment;
  2. An updated Curriculum Vitae (CV), including relevant qualifications, professional experience and contact details of referees;
  3. Evidence of relevant previous assignments demonstrating experience in GRM development, SOP development, governance, social safeguards or related areas; and
  4. Any other information considered relevant to demonstrating the Consultant's suitability for the assignment.
  5. The Individual Consultant may associate with other suitably qualified experts, as necessary, to provide complementary technical expertise required for the assignment. The proposed experts shall have relevant qualifications and experience appropriate to their respective areas of responsibility. The Individual Consultant shall remain the lead consultant and shall be fully responsible and accountable for the overall coordination, quality and timely delivery of all assignment outputs.

Consultants are encouraged to provide sufficient information in their CVs and supporting documentation to demonstrate their specific experience relevant to this assignment.

9. Selection Method

The Individual Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection (ICS) method under the applicable World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers.

The selection will be based on the qualifications and experience of the individual Consultant relevant to the assignment.

10. Conflict of Interest

Consultants shall be required to disclose any actual or potential conflict of interest in relation to the assignment. Consultants will be required to comply with the applicable World Bank provisions relating to conflict of interest.

11. Submission of Expressions of Interest

Expressions of Interest, together with the Consultant's CV and supporting information, should be submitted to:

The Permanent Secretary
Ministry of Local Government and Rural Development
P.O Box
Lusaka, Zambia

Attention: Head Procurement

Email: Jacob.Masatunya@gov.zm, Gretchen.Mushinge@mlgrd.gov.zm

Closing Date: 2nd Septe,ber, 2026
Closing Time: 14:00 hours CAT

The subject line should clearly state:

“Expression of Interest – Individual Consultant to Develop GRM Standard Operating Procedures and Tools for Local Authorities – ZDSP.”

Only shortlisted/selected Consultants will be contacted.

The Government of Indonesia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of Inclusive Service Delivery and Digital Transformation in Indonesia (Loan No. IBRD-95200), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

To respond to the increasing needs and challenges in population administration and to utilize the strategic role of accurate population data, the Government of Indonesia has initiated comprehensive efforts to modernize and strengthen its system. This commitment is reflected in the launch of the project "ID for Inclusive Service Delivery and Digital Transformation in Indonesia," which aims to improve the population and civil registration framework and introduce secure digital identity solutions. Through this initiative, Indonesia seeks to ensure that all citizens and residents can access inclusive, efficient, and digitally integrated public and private services, thereby supporting national development goals and digital transformation.

In general, the scope of work for this consultant service includes:

I. Implementation of an Independent Public Satisfaction Survey (IKM). The Consulting Firm shall design and implement the Public Satisfaction Index (IKM) survey on population administration services, to be conducted twice:

  1. in 2026 as a baseline measurement, and

The Consulting Firm shall develop comprehensive recommendations to strengthen DG Dukcapil’s integrated Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system, ensuring that both citizens and institutional users have access to feedback mechanisms that are secure, traceable, and responsive, thereby supporting citizen-centric service delivery and enhancing service satisfaction.

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for Supporting the Operation and Development of the Competitive Trading Bilateral Contract Market (CTBCM) In Pakistan’s Power Sector.

Reference No. PK-MOE-566558-CS-QCBS-CTBCM

 

The Ministry of Energy (Power Division) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Electricity Distribution Efficiency Improvement Project (EDEIP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for engagement of a consultancy firm for Independent System and Market Operator of Pakistan (ISMO) for supporting the operation and development of the Competitive Trading Bilateral Contract Market (CTBCM) in Pakistan’s power sector.

 

The consulting services (“the Services”) include key experts to undertake multiple tasks for supporting the operation and development of the CTBCM according to the scope provided in the detailed Terms of Reference (TOR). The TOR for the assignment can be downloaded from https://power.gov.pk/ or www.ismo.gov.pk.

 

The Program Implementing Unit (PIU), Ministry of Energy (Power Division) now invites EOI from eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants are required to provide information demonstrating their qualification and relevant experience to perform the Services described in the TOR. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

 

Shortlisting criteria for the Consultants include:

  • The firm must have been duly incorporated and operational for a minimum period of ten (10) years as of the date of submission in the same business (documented evidence showing years in business such as certificate of incorporation etc. must be provided).
  • The firm shall provide evidence of at least two prior assignments of comparable nature, scope and complexity, demonstrating relevant experience.
  • The firm shall demonstrate that its proposed team, supported by adequate back-end resources, possesses the requisite qualifications and experience to effectively deliver the assignment.

                                                                                                                                              

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers February, 2025 (“the Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub- consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, whereas each partner within the JV shall meet the qualification and experience requirement for the assigned role, if selected.

 

The Consultant will be selected in accordance with the “Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS)” method set out in the Procurement Regulations of the World Bank for IPF Borrower February, 2025.

Name of Project: “Innovative Social Protection System for Inclusion of Vulnerable People” (INSON)

 

Financing Agreement No. 7555-UZ / Grant Agreement No. TF C4589-UZ

 

Assignment Title: Supporting the Introduction of Care Manager Function in Uzbekistan

 

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): UZ-INSON-CS-QCBS-2.1.6.2.

 

The Republic of Uzbekistan has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Innovative Social Protection System for Inclusion of Vulnerable People (INSON) Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

The consulting services (“Services”) include support for the design and first-phase implementation of the Care Manager function within the National Agency for Social Protection under the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan, based on relevant international experience and good practices. The Consultant will support the development of the Care Management concept, professional and service standards, comprehensive needs assessment and individual care planning tools, referral and service coordination mechanisms, monitoring and KPI frameworks, training and professional development arrangements, and related methodological and operational documents. The assignment includes training of at least 210 Care Managers, development and implementation of a Training of Trainers (ToT) framework and preparation of a national group of thirty (30) trainers selected by NASP, as well as hands-on implementation support in Tashkent City and the Samarkand, Fergana, Kashkadarya, Navoi, and Khorezm regions. Subsequent adoption and institutionalization of the Care Management system will be led by NASP.

 

The total duration of the assignment is 12 months, during six (6) months of which the expert team will be required to be present in the Republic of Uzbekistan.

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following link:

 

https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Cxy8Xz8WD0bp98-peZGJuUF3gUYJPTRg/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=104755491226149341341&rtpof=true&sd=true

 

The National Agency for Social Protection (NASP) under the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information (including description of relevant assignments and references from previous clients) demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:  

  • At least five (5) years of institutional experience in social protection, social services, Care Management, case management, integrated care, long-term care, medical-social services, person-centered care, or a closely related field.
  • Demonstrated experience in the design, development, piloting, implementation support, or improvement of Care Management, case management, long-term care, integrated care, or comparable coordinated service delivery models.
  • Experience in developing operational and methodological instruments, including assessment tools, individual care plans, service pathways, referral protocols, professional or service standards, standard operating procedures, monitoring tools, competency frameworks, and related documents.
  • Experience in training, Training of Trainers, mentoring, supervision, or professional development in the social protection, social services, care, health, rehabilitation, or related sectors.
  • Experience in monitoring service quality, safety, effectiveness, and implementation results, including the use of feedback from practitioners and service users to improve methodologies and tools.
  • Experience in supporting public institutions and working with government bodies, service providers, non-governmental organizations, private providers, and other stakeholders.
  • Sufficient organizational, technical, and managerial capacity to perform the assignment.
  • Experience in assignments supported by international development organizations and in applying relevant international standards and good practices will be an advantage.

 

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

FOR THE ACCELERATING SUSTAINABLE AND CLEAN ENERGY ACCESS TRANSFORMATION IN ESWATINI (ASCENT) PROJECT

Request for Expression of Interest (REOI)

 

Eswatini Electricity Company (EEC)

(Government of the Kingdom of Eswatini)

Consultancy Services for a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) Grid Integration and Planning Study

 

First date of publication:           06 August 2026

Country:                                      Kingdom of Eswatini

Name of Project:                        Accelerating Sustainable and Clean Energy Access Transformation in Eswatini (ASCENT Eswatini) Project

Sector:                                          Energy Sector

Project ID No.:                            P508960

Reference:                                   SZ-ECC-561947-CS-CQS

Assignment Title:                       Consulting Services for a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) Grid Integration and Planning Study

 

 

  1. The Government of the Kingdom of Eswatini (GoKE) has received financing from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD), the International Development Agency (IDA) and grant funding from the Global Public Good (GPG) Facility, which are all under the World Bank. The received financing is for the purposes of implementing the Accelerating Sustainable and Clean Energy Access Transformation in Eswatini (ASCENT Eswatini) Project (P508960) (the Project), with the involvement of the Ministry of Natural Resources and Energy, as set out in the Loan Agreement, Financing Agreement, Grant Agreement and Project Agreements.

 

  1. The EEC now invites Expressions of Interest (EOI) from interested and eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to provide consulting services for a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) Grid Integration and Planning Study.

 

  1. The Consultant shall undertake, but not necessarily be limited to the following tasks:

 

      1. Review of the Existing Energy Power System: Conduct a high-level review of the entire EEC transmission network,
      2. BESS Technology Assessment: Evaluate suitable utility-scale BESS technologies,
      3. Assessment of BESS Grid Applications: Analyze the technical role of BESS in the entire EEC transmission network,
      4. Solar PV and BESS Hybrid Assessment: Assess the benefits of co-locating BESS with committed solar PV projects,
      5. Power System Modelling and Impact Studies: Conduct detailed power system modelling, stability studies and network impact analysis to evaluate the combined impact of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) and Flexible AC Transmission Systems (FACTS) devices on the EEC grid.
      6. Optimal BESS and FACTS Devices Location and Sizing: Determine optimal siting, sizing and operational configuration of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS),
      7. Inverter Technology Assessment: Evaluate grid-following and grid-forming applications for BESS,
      8. Grid Resilience and Restoration: Assess the potential role of BESS and FACTS devices in enhancing system resilience,
      9. Economic Assessment: Conduct cost-benefit analysis of Bess deployment options, sensitivity analysis on key parameters, estimate total projects costs, assess financial viability of BESS under ownership and commercial models (public utility ownership, IPP/PPP structures and hybrid models),
      10. Environmental and Social Safeguards: Conduct a preliminary environmental and social screening of candidate BESS sites,
      11. Deployment Strategy and Roadmap: Develop a comprehensive and integrated deployment strategy and implementation roadmap for BESS and FACTS technologies.

 

 

  1. Interested consultants must provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform all the services. The following documents shall also be submitted along with the EOI applications by all the consulting firms including each member of JV firms:
      • Copies of certificates of incorporation/registration of the consulting firms
      • Annual financial records of the firm for the last 5 years
      • Corporate profile of the firm with quality assurance plan, e.g. ISO 9001, information on organizational strength (Organization structure, number of permanent professional staffs and their expertise, qualifications and number of total staff), evidence of availability of licensed power system analysis software, including but not limited to: PSS®E, DIgSILENT Power Factory, ETAP, PSCAD or equivalent software required for execution of the assignment.

 

  1. The qualifications and shortlisting criteria are:
  • At least ten (10) years’ experience in grid planning, stability, storage, or renewable integration studies.
  • At least five (5) relevant assignments in Africa.
  • Demonstrated experience of at least one (1) relevant assignment in BESS integration, including siting, sizing, and grid impact analysis in Africa.
  • Proven experience of at least one (1) relevant assignment in FACTS devices analysis (e.g., STATCOM, SVC) for voltage control and stability in Africa.
  • Prove Experience with utility transmission networks.
  1. The purpose of this EOI is to establish the consultant who has the best qualifications for the assignment and to invite that consultant to submit a technical and financial proposal. All responses shall be assessed for completeness. The following shall be assessed on a Yes/No basis to determine a PASS or FAIL result; ten (10) years’ experience in grid planning, stability, storage, or renewable integration studies, five (5) relevant assignments in grid planning, stability, storage, or renewable integration studies in Africa, demonstrated experience of at least one (1) relevant assignment in BESS integration, including siting, sizing, and grid impact analysis in Africa and proven experience of at least one (1) relevant assignment in FACTS devices analysis (e.g., STATCOM, SVC) for voltage control and stability in Africa and experience with utility transmission networks.

 

The consultant who has attained the highest pass rate result shall be invited to submit a request for proposal based on the following weighted aspect:

  • General corporate experience; [15]
  • Specific experience in BESS planning and integration studies; [25]
  • Power system planning and stability studies experience; [20]
  • FACTS technology assessment and deployment experience; [15]
  • Experience working with electricity utilities; [15]
  • Regional (African) experience. [10]

 

  1. In order to substantiate the aforementioned consulting jobs/contracts, the Consultant shall submit the Completion Certificates or End User Certificate from clients depicting description of services provided. All Completion Certificate or End User Certificates should be in English; Completion Certificates/ End User Certificates in other languages should be translated and notarized. Incomplete Consulting Contracts will not be taken into account and hence will not be evaluated.

 

  1. Consultants may associate with other consultants to enhance their qualifications. For a JV/consortium, the qualifications and experience of the members may be combined to meet the qualification requirements. The Lead Partner shall demonstrate substantial relevant experience and shall be responsible for contract performance. Consortium members may combine qualifications and experience to meet the overall qualification requirements.

 

  1. All submittal from the consulting firms shall be in English language.

 

  1. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.15 to 3.16 of the Seventh edition of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers dated September 2025, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

 

  1. The Consultant(s) shall be evaluated and shortlisted based on the qualifications, experience and capability. Qualifications and Experience of key personnel will not be evaluated at this stage. The shortlisted consultant will subsequently be invited to submit Technical and Financial Proposals and the Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant Qualification Selection (CQS) method as per the Seventh edition of Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers dated September 2025.

 

  1. Interested eligible consultants may obtain further information by sending an email to the address below or visiting during office hours from 10.00 to 16.00 hrs. The Terms of Reference for the proposed consulting services can be accessed at the link below:

 

https://www.eec.co.sz/electricity/projects/ascent/docs/Battery_Energy_Storage_System_BESS_Grid_Intergration_and_Planning_Study_TORs.pdf

ASSIGNMENT TITLE:  CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR WEBTRUST AUDIT AND AATL RECOGNITION PROGRAMME FOR THE UGANDA NATIONAL PUBLIC KEY INFRASTRUCTURE

 

The Government of Uganda, represented by the National Information Technology Authority - Uganda (NITA-U), has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Uganda Digital Acceleration Project - Government Network (UDAP-GOVNET) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consultancy services for Webtrust Audit and AATL Recognition Programme for the Uganda National Public Key Infrastructure

 

The consulting services (“the Services”) include consultancy services for Webtrust Audit and AATL Recognition Programme for the Uganda National Public Key Infrastructure.

 

The objective of the assignment is to obtain independent, internationally recognized assurance and trust-list recognition for Uganda’s National Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), thereby strengthening its credibility, security and interoperability with internationally recognized digital trust frameworks. Specifically, the assignment will engage a licensed and independent WebTrust for Certification Authorities practitioner to conduct a formal audit, including evidence review, remediation tracking and certification support for one year; prepare, submit and coordinate the Adobe Approved Trust List (AATL) recognition process to facilitate document-signing trust and interoperability, including coverage of the annual programme fee for one year; and provide ongoing certification maintenance and query-response support throughout the one-year assurance period.

 

The Implementation period of the assignment is Five (5) Months from the date of signing the contract.

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: https://www.nita.go.ug/opportunities/bids-and-tenders

 

The National Information Technology Authority - Uganda now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The Shortlisting Criteria for the firm’s capacity and experience are:

 

  1. The firm should have completed at least Two (2) WebTrust for Certification Authorities audits or equivalent assessments (e.g., ETSI EN 319 401/411) for CA/PKI environments within the last five (5) years.
  2. Submit the firm’s organogram to demonstrate the firm’s technical and managerial capability;
  3. Presence of appropriate skills among staff; Lead WebTrust Auditor / Practitioner and AATL AATL Technical Liaison Specialist (please do not submit CVs and biodata of experts at this stage).

 

The attention of interested consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.15 and 3.16, of the World Bank’s ‘Procurement in Investment Project Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, Seventh Edition September 2025 (Procurement in investment Project Financing; Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

 

A consultant will be selected in accordance with the Least Cost Selection (LCS) method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations “Procurement in Investment Project Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, Seventh Edition September 2025”.

 

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours at the address below 08:00 to 17:00 hours from Monday to Friday at the address given below.

AVIS À MANIFESTATION D'INTÉRÊT

 

« Recrutement d'un Consultant Individuel International pour l'élaboration de la cartographie des ressources régionales et nationales pour la prévention, la détection et la réponse aux urgences sanitaires »

 

 

  1. Contexte

Le Gouvernement de la République du Tchad a reçu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour la mise en œuvre du Projet de Sécurité Sanitaire en Afrique de l'Ouest et du Centre (HeSP) et entend utiliser une partie de ce financement pour recruter un Consultant Individuel International chargé de réaliser la cartographie des ressources régionales et nationales destinées à la prévention, à la détection et à la réponse aux urgences sanitaires.

Cette mission s'inscrit dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre de la Sous-composante 1.1 « Gouvernance, planification et intendance de la sécurité sanitaire » et vise à doter le pays d'un outil stratégique permettant d'améliorer la planification, la coordination intersectorielle et la mobilisation rapide des ressources selon l'approche « Une Seule Santé (One Health) ».

  1. Objet de la mission

L'objectif général de la mission est d'élaborer une cartographie complète, structurée et opérationnelle des ressources régionales et nationales dédiées à la prévention, à la détection et à la réponse aux urgences sanitaires au Tchad.

À ce titre, le consultant sera notamment chargé de :

  • réaliser un inventaire exhaustif des ressources humaines, matérielles, financières, institutionnelles et informationnelles disponibles ;
  • analyser les capacités existantes par secteur, niveau administratif et capacité du RSI (2005) ;
  • identifier les mécanismes de coordination entre les secteurs de la santé humaine, animale et environnementale ainsi qu'avec les partenaires techniques et financiers ;
  • identifier les insuffisances, les duplications et les opportunités de mutualisation des ressources ;
  • élaborer une cartographie géoréférencée des ressources et produire les tableaux de bord correspondants ;
  • proposer des recommandations opérationnelles visant à renforcer la coordination, la planification et la mobilisation des ressources ;
  • faciliter l'organisation de l'atelier national de validation et finaliser les livrables de la mission.
  • La durée prévisionnelle de la mission est de quarante-cinq (45) jours calendaires.
  1.  Profil recherché

Le consultant devra satisfaire aux qualifications suivantes :

  • être titulaire au minimum d'un diplôme universitaire de niveau Master en santé publique, épidémiologie, médecine vétérinaire, sciences de l'environnement, gouvernance sanitaire, géomatique/SIG ou tout autre domaine pertinent ;
  • justifier d'au moins dix (10) années d'expérience professionnelle dans les domaines de la santé publique, de la sécurité sanitaire, de l'épidémiologie ou de la planification sanitaire ;
  • avoir réalisé au moins une mission similaire de cartographie des ressources sanitaires, d'évaluation des capacités du système de santé ou des capacités liées au RSI (2005) ;
  • disposer d'une expérience avérée dans l'approche « Une Seule Santé » et dans la coordination multisectorielle ;
  • maîtriser les outils de cartographie et les systèmes d'information géographique (SIG) appliqués à la santé publique ;
  • avoir une expérience de travail en Afrique subsaharienne ; une expérience en Afrique centrale ou dans la région du Sahel constituera un atout ;
  • posséder d'excellentes capacités d'analyse, de rédaction et de communication en français ; la connaissance de l'anglais constitue un avantage.
  1. Composition du dossier de candidature

Les consultants intéressés devront fournir :

  • une lettre de manifestation d'intérêt signée ;
  • un curriculum vitae détaillé, daté et signé, mettant en évidence les qualifications et les expériences pertinentes pour la mission ;
  • les copies des diplômes et certificats pertinents ;
  • les références de missions similaires réalisées, accompagnées des justificatifs disponibles (copies des pages de garde et de signature des contrats, attestations de bonne exécution, certificats de bonne fin ou tout autre document probant) ;
  • tout document permettant d'apprécier les qualifications et l'expérience du consultant.

Les références fournies pourront faire l'objet de vérifications auprès des maîtres d'ouvrage concernés.

4. Méthode de sélection

Le consultant sera recruté conformément aux dispositions du Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant un Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) de la Banque mondiale, édition septembre 2025, selon la méthode de Sélection de Consultants Individuels (CI).

5. Dépôt des manifestations d’intérêt

Les manifestations d’intérêt rédigées en langue française doivent être déposées sous pli fermé et/ou transmises par voie électronique à l’adresse indiquée ci-dessous au plus tard le 03 septembre 2026 à 16 heures 00mn (heure de N’Djamena), avec la mention :

« Manifestation d'Intérêt pour le recrutement d'un Consultant Individuel International chargé de l'élaboration de la cartographie des ressources régionales et nationales pour la prévention, la détection et la réponse aux urgences sanitaires »

Bureau de la coordination Nationale de l’UCP-HeSP sise au quartier BOLOLO en face de la SNE à l'attention de : Thierry Madjitoloum TOINA, Coordonnateur National Tél : (+235) 66 26 73 85/63 07 53 58/66 56 11 05/66 29 61 52/ ou par mail à l'adresse suivante : thierrytoina@outlook.com / adoumtomabakar@outlook.com / fatimedarayya@outlook.com

 

  1. Informations complémentaires

Les consultants intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations complémentaires et consulter les Termes de Référence aux heures ouvrables auprès de l’Unité de Coordination des Projets (UCP) à l’adresse ci-dessus citée.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

 

Country: Indonesia

Name of Project: Indonesia Health System Strengthening (IHSS) Project

Loan No.: IBRD Loan No. 9626

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for Legal Compliance and Documentation

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): ID-COMP 4 IHSS-550314-CS-QCBS

Date: August 18, 2026

 

  1. The Ministry of Health (MoH) of the Republic of Indonesia has received loan financing from the World Bank to support the implementation of the Indonesia Health System Strengthening (IHSS) Project, with total funding amounting to EUR 3.7 billion. The IHSS Project (“the Project”) is a national initiative aimed at strengthening primary healthcare, referral services, and public health laboratories through the provision of medical equipment and capacity building across health facilities nationwide. To support the timely and accountable implementation of the Project, the MoH intends to engage a qualified law firm to provide legal advisory services, ensure compliance with applicable laws and regulations, and strengthen the Project’s documentation and record-keeping systems. The assignment is intended to promote consistent implementation of sound documentation, indexing, and legal compliance practices throughout the Project lifecycle.
  2. The consulting services (“the Services”) comprise comprehensive legal and compliance support to the MoH for the implementation of the IHSS Project. The selected firm will assist the MoH in strengthening legal compliance and establishing robust documentation management, record-keeping, and indexing systems to promote sound governance and effective risk mitigation throughout the Project. The firm will conduct ongoing legal and compliance reviews across all Project implementing teams, including SOPHI, SIHREN, InPULS, and project management activities, regardless of the financing sources. In addition, the firm will provide practical recommendations and capacity-building support to MoH personnel to institutionalize a strong compliance culture and systematic documentation practices. The scope of services will include, but not be limited to, the following: i) Legal Compliance and Regulatory Review; ii) Documentation Management, Record-Keeping, and Indexing; iii) Compliance Monitoring and Reporting; iv) Legal and Regulatory Alignment; v) Governance and Risk Management Support; and vi) Training and Awareness. The assignment is expected to require approximately 162 professional staff-months over the implementation period. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: https://s.kemkes.go.id/LCDCIHSS
  3. The Services for Legal Compliance and Documentation Consultancy Firm is expected to commence in November 2026 and conclude by April 2028.
  4. The Ministry of Health (MoH) now invites eligible firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide sufficient information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services (including the name and location/country of the Client, type and scope of services provided, period of contract, contract amount, role of the firm, starting and completion dates, key output delivered and experts involved in the assignment).

The shortlisting criteria are:

a. Legal Status and Registration: 

The consulting firm shall be a legally registered entity with a valid business license and shall provide evidence of such legal registration. The firm shall possess relevant national and/or international accreditations or certifications applicable to the scope of the assignment (e.g., ISO 37001, ISO 9001, or equivalent).

b. Core business and years in business:

Minimum seven (7) years of proven experience in legal advisory services or related services, which include, but not limited to any of the following areas: regulatory review and/or compliance, contract management, contract dispute resolutions, and governance frameworks.

c. Relevant experience:

1. Demonstrated experience in providing legal services to government agencies/SOEs, international organizations, and/or private entities in any of the following areas:

a) legal compliance review of procurement, contract or project documentation;

The Government of Somaliland (GoSL), through the Ministry of Local Government and Urban Development (MoLGUD), is implementing the World Bank-financed Bulsho Project – Strengthening Community Institutions for Social Cohesion, Inclusion and Resilience (P508408).

The Bulsho Project aims to strengthen community and local government institutions to enhance social cohesion, inclusion, and resilience. It places citizens and communities at the center of governance and supports improved service delivery, stronger citizen-government relations, and inclusive and participatory local governance.

To support effective project implementation, MoLGUD intends to recruit a qualified and experienced Social Safeguarding Officer within the Project Implementation Unit (PIU) to provide technical leadership on social risk management, social inclusion, and safeguarding in accordance with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF).

2. SCOPE OF THE ASSIGNMENT

The PIU Bulsho Social Safeguarding Officer will provide overall technical guidance, oversight, and quality assurance on social risk management, social inclusion, and gender mainstreaming across the Bulsho Project. The Officer will ensure that project-supported processes, including the Local Social Contract Platform (LSCP), Citizens’ Charters, participatory community planning, and matching grants, advance the Project’s social development and inclusion objectives, particularly the meaningful participation of women, youth, minorities, IDPs, and other marginalized groups.

The Officer will support compliance with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), Environmental and Social Commitment Plan (ESCP), Project Operations Manual (POM), and other applicable social safeguard instruments. Key areas will include social risk assessment and mitigation, stakeholder and community engagement, gender and social inclusion, grievance redress mechanisms (GRM), SEA/SH risk mitigation, social screening, capacity building, field monitoring, reporting, and quality assurance.

The detailed scope of services, responsibilities, deliverables, reporting arrangements, and other requirements are provided in the attached Terms of Reference (TOR).

The successful candidate shall meet the following minimum qualifications and experience:

  • A university degree in Sociology, Social Development, Gender Studies, Anthropology, Development Studies, Social Work, or a related field. A Master’s degree is an advantage.
  • A minimum of six (6) years of professional experience in social development, social inclusion, or social safeguards.
  • At least four (4) years of experience in donor-funded projects, with proven application of the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) or equivalent standards.
  • Demonstrated experience in providing technical guidance, oversight, or quality assurance for participatory planning, inclusion strategies, or social risk management.
  • Experience working with government institutions, preferably in fragile or conflict-affected settings.
  • Strong analytical and advisory skills in social risk management, inclusion, and gender mainstreaming.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop guidance tools, training materials, and capacity-building programs.
  • Strong communication, facilitation, organizational, and coordination skills, with the ability to engage effectively with government institutions, development partners, and communities.
  • In-depth knowledge and understanding of the World Bank ESF, ESCP, and related environmental and social instruments.
  • Familiarity with Somaliland’s social dynamics, local governance structures, and institutional context.
  • Good understanding of cross-cutting issues, including gender equality, social inclusion, resilience, and conflict sensitivity.
  • High standards of professional integrity, accountability, and ethical conduct.
  • Excellent command of English and Somali, including reading, writing, and presentation skills.

The PIU Bulsho Social Safeguarding Officer will report to the Bulsho PIU Project Manager and work closely with other relevant PIU members.

The consulting services (hereinafter referred to as the “Services”) envisage the implementation of the program of strengthening capacity of PJSC “Ukrhydroenergo” (UHE) in the area of Environmental, Social, and Corporate Governance (ESG), which shall include two complementary components: () conducting basic ESG trainings for a broad audience of UHE employees to promote a general understanding of ESG - integrating ESG aspects into UHE’s corporate management practices, including the European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS) as part of the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) and the Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive (CSDDD); and (ii) conducting in-depth practical sessions for employees directly involved in the implementation of ESG principles and reporting at UHE according to European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS) and other standards of International Financial Institutions  (IFI), as well as in the planning and implementation of projects using E&S risk management tools.

Components of the assignment:

() Component 1 – basic ESG trainings for a broad audience: development of a basic understanding of ESG concept; implementation and integration of environmental, social, and corporate governance (ESG) practices into all aspects of the Company's operations; integration of new reporting into business processes; ESG risk assessment, double materiality assessment, and understanding of the greenhouse gas emissions calculation process, including for taking them into account in cross-border electricity trade using UHE border carbon adjustment mechanism, among approximately 100 employees in key corporate functions.

(ii) Component 2 – In-depth capacity building on ESMS and E&S risk management at the project level: Strengthening the practical capacity of approximately 30–40 employees directly involved in implementing UHE’s environmental and social policies, as well as in project planning and development, in particular through the development and implementation of an Environmental and Social Management System (ESMS) and risk management tools at the project level.

(iii) Preparing reports by each component separately and a consolidated report on the follow-up activities based on the results of the conducted training sessions.

The contract is scheduled to begin on 30.10.2026, and its approximate completion period is 6 months from the effective date of the contract.

More details on the Services are provided in the Terms of Reference that can be uploaded by this link:  https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/10YpUAT00aLipxY_GQPYQ1_sfAM_vFjYo?usp=drive_link

It will not be discussed with the Consultants at this stage, and any changes, if appropriate, will be agreed upon with the most qualified Consultant at later stages of the selection process.

The most qualified Consultant will be selected based on the qualification criteria listed below.

PJSC “Ukrhydroenergo” now invites qualified consulting firms (the “Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the specified Services.  

The interested Consultants shall provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The criteria for ranking the interested Consultants are as follows:

The Consultant is a legal entity duly registered in accordance with the laws of its country of registration.

The Consultant’s qualifications shall meet the following requirements:

Mandatory qualification:

  • Experience in completing at least 2 (two) assignments within projects financed by international financial institutions (the World Bank, the EBRD, the EIB, or other international financial institutions) starting from 2020, including at least one assignment related to ESG/E&S/sustainable development;
  • Proven experience in organizing and conducting training events (training sessions, seminars, workshops) in the field of environmental, social, and/or corporate governance (ESG / E&S / sustainable development)—at least 20 events since 2020, including both online and offline formats;
  • At least 5 (five) developed training programs, methodological manuals or templates in the field of sustainable development / ESG since 2020;
  • Implementation of at least 3 (three) assignments/contracts for building institutional capacity on ESG issues for government agencies, state-owned enterprises, or large companies since 2020;
  • At least 2 (two) assignments, within which the Consultant explained or implemented the World Bank’s ESF requirements, the EBRD standards or EU directives on sustainable development (CSRD, CSDDD, WFD);

ALBANIA

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

(CONSULTING SERVICES)

Selection of Individual Consultant

Climate Resilience and Agriculture Development Project in Albania

Project ID Number:  No.: P178715

IBRD Loan Number: 94890

Assignment Title: “M&E Consultant of PMT”  

(Ref. No. AL-MARD-560551-CS-INDV)”

The World Bank is assisting the Government of Albania (GoA) with the financing of the Climate Resilience and Agriculture Development project (CRAD). This project aims to increase competitiveness and climate resilience of priority agri-food value chains. The expected outputs from the project are: (i) increased supply/sales to local agri-food businesses, (ii) increased agricultural productivity and production, lower costs and extended production season (iii) improved traceability, farmer’s market integration and the compliance with food safety and quality requirements, (iv) evidence-based decision making for resilience and sustainable agri-food systems.

The Project consists of the following components, which will support the project objective:

  1. Promoting Climate Smart Agriculture and Access to Markets
  2. Enhancing Compliance with Food Safety and Quality Standards
  3. Strengthening Evidence-based Analysis Capacity of MARD and Municipalities

The services required to be contracted aim to support the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development (MARD) in ensuring successful implementation of the contract “M&E Consultant of PMT”.

The Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development (MARD) is the lead implementation agency for this Project (CRAD) and publishes this Request for Expression of Interest with the aim of selecting an individual consultant as M&E Consultant of PMT who will be part (a team member) of the PMT and he/she will support the PMT in monitring and evalution issue compliance in the implementation of Project activities.

Objective of the Consultancy and Scope of Work

The primary objective of the Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Specialist consultancy is to support the effective implementation of the Climate Resilience and Agriculture Development Project by establishing and operationalizing robust monitoring and evaluation systems. The M&E Specialist will ensure that project activities across all components are tracked, analyzed, and reported in alignment with the project’s development objectives of increasing competitiveness and climate resilience of priority agri-food value chains. The role will contribute to evidence-based decision-making, facilitate adaptive management, and strengthen institutional capacity at the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development (MARD) and municipal levels, with a particular focus on stakeholder engagement and local context.

Key activities and responsibilities include:

  1. Develop and implement a comprehensive M&E framework for the project, including clear indicators, data collection methodologies, and reporting protocols, in accordance with the project results framework and World Bank guidelines.
  2. Coordinate and oversee the collection, validation, and analysis of quantitative and qualitative data related to project outputs, outcomes, and impacts across all components, including productivity improvements, irrigation and drainage upgrades, compliance with food safety standards, and institutional strengthening.
  3. Support the MARD and municipalities in building capacity for consistent and comprehensive data collection, management, and analysis, ensuring integration of gender-disaggregated and beneficiary feedback indicators.
  4. Facilitate participatory monitoring processes, including the establishment and engagement of local monitoring groups composed of farmers, agri-food businesses, and other stakeholders, to enhance transparency and accountability in project implementation.
  5. Prepare periodic progress reports, evaluation summaries, and presentations for project management, government counterparts, and the World Bank, highlighting achievements, challenges, and recommendations for adaptive management.
  6. Contribute to the preparation and review of project documentation required for compliance with environmental and social safeguards, including monitoring of citizen engagement activities and grievance redress mechanisms.
  7. Provide technical support for scaling up digital tools such as the Irrigation and Drainage Management Information System (IDMIS) and GIS mapping, and ensure their effective use in monitoring project activities at municipal and central levels.
  8. Liaise with local stakeholders, including beneficiaries, community representatives, and implementing agencies, to ensure timely and accurate information flow and promote inclusive participation in M&E activities.

This list of duties and responsibilities is not exhaustive, and the consultant may be required to perform other related tasks as assigned by the designated supervisor.

Required Experience and Qualifications

The Consultant shall possess the following qualifications and experience:

  • At least a university degree, preferably a Master's degree, in Economics, Business Administration, Statistics, Public Administration, Agricultural and Rural Development, Social Sciences, or another relevant discipline.
  • A minimum of fifteen (15) years of overall professional experience.
  • At least seven (7) years of demonstrated experience in the design, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development projects and program in the field of agriculture, food safety and irrigation.
  • At least ten (10) years of professional experience working on projects financed by international development organizations, preferably in the agriculture and rural development sector.
  • Previous experience with World Bank-financed projects will be considered a strong advantage.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of results-based monitoring and evaluation methodologies and data analysis techniques.
  • Excellent analytical, report writing, and presentation skills.
  • Excellent command of written and spoken Albanian and English.
  • Strong interpersonal, communication, and teamwork skills.

Applicants that fulfill the minimum qualification requirements will be further evaluated based on the below evaluation grid for the position:

Evaluated expertise

Points

General Experience

30

Adequacy for the assignment

60

Language and computer skills

10

Total

100

The consultant will be selected based on Selection of Individual Consultant (IC) in accordance with the procedures set out in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Procurement in Investment Project Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services July 2016 (revised November 2020).

The initial duration of the assignment is 12 months, with a probation period of 3 months, from contract signing and/or entry into force of the contract, with the option of renewal for the entire Project implementation period (38 months), based on satisfactory performance.  The type of contract for this assignment is Time Based Contract.  The Consultant M&E expert shall be engaged on a full-time basis.

Interested local Consultants may obtain further information concerning the Terms of Reference at the official website of MARD: https://bujqesia.gov.al/projekti-qendrueshmeria-ndaj-klimes-dhe-zhvillimit-ne-bujqesi/, or at the address below, during office hours 08:00 to 16:30 (Monday to Thursday) and 08:00 to 14:00 on Friday.

The Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development (MARD) invites interested individuals to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested candidates should provide: (i) motivation letter, underlining their advantages concerning this position, (ii)   Curriculum Vitae, as well as, (iii) information that indicates that the candidates have required qualifications to carry out the Consulting Services, and (iv) various references.

All documents should be submitted in English language.

Expressions of Interest (EoIs) must be delivered no later than September 03, 2026 hardcopy (in person or by mail) to the address below, within office hours, and/or electronically at the below e-mail address.

 

Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development

Adr: Blv. "Dëshmorët e Kombit", Nr. 2, 1001, Tirana, Albania

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

 Loan No./Credit No./ Grant No.: IDA-7355-KE

 Assignment Title:                 BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT SERVICES (BDS) PROVIDERS FOR REFUGEES

Reference No:                        MSEA/NYOTA/NCB/11/2026-207

  1. The Government’s Bottom-up Economic Transformation Agenda (BETA) places significant focus on the Micro, Small, and Enterprises (MSE) Sector by prioritizing financial inclusion for MSEs, adopting a value chain approach to MSE products, and promoting sustainable job creation through the sector.

 

  1. In line with this agenda, the Government of Kenya (GoK) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the National Youth Opportunities Towards Advancement (NYOTA) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

  1. The Consulting services (“the Services”) include Business Development Services (BDS) to establish a foundation and systems for the sustained creation of opportunities for employment, earnings, and savings to improve economic empowerment among youth in refugee counties, Garissa and Turkana, in the Republic of Kenya. The Micro and Small Enterprises Authority (“Authority”) is seeking the services of a qualified Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) to design, pilot and deliver a comprehensive Business Development Services (BDS) package targeted at refugee youth in Kenya. The targeted beneficiaries of the project are Kenyan youth aged 18 to 29 who are unemployed, have experienced extended periods of unemployment, or are currently engaged in vulnerable jobs. For persons living with disabilities (PWDs), the upper age limit is extended to 35 years.The educational level of the targeted beneficiaries ranges from Form 4 and below. The role of the Business Development Services Providers is to deliver a practical BDS package with clearly defined modules, duration, number of sessions, and expected outputs as specified in the Deliverables tailored to refugee community youth in Dadaab and Kakuma with a particular focus on social emotional and business skills training, as well as mentorship. This package may include a face-to-face training program that builds entrepreneurial mindset, resilience and core business competencies as a prerequisite input to BDS and financing pathways. The services will include one-to-one and small-group coaching to identify viable opportunities.

 

  1. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found on the following website: www.msea.go.ke

 

  1. The Micro and Small Enterprises Authority (“Authority”) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are

 

    1. Core business and years in business: The firm shall be registered/incorporated as non-governmental organization with the core business in Business Development Services (BDS), entrepreneurship development, livelihoods support, youth economic empowerment, or related interventions/fields for at least five (5) years.
    2. Relevant experience: (i)The firm must have successfully undertaken at least two (2) assignments of a similar nature within the last five (5) years, including experience in refugee, humanitarian, displacement-affected, or other low-resource settings. Experience in Kenya, particularly in refugee settings, from 2018 to date. (ii) The firm must demonstrate experience in developing, adapting, or customizing BDS, entrepreneurship, livelihoods, or related training curricula to meet the contextual, cultural, socioeconomic, and methodological needs of refugee beneficiary communities. (iii) The firm must demonstrate experience in implementing ongoing programmes in the refugee camps, (Kakuma/Kalobeyei and/or Dadaab) including the delivery of Business Development Services (BDS), entrepreneurship, livelihoods, or youth economic empowerment interventions.
    3. Technical and managerial capability of the firm: (i) The firm must demonstrate ownership, access to, or the technical capacity to develop and deploy a digital platform that is accessible to beneficiaries and can facilitate the registration, attendance, participation, progress monitoring, and reporting of youth beneficiaries. (ii) The firm must demonstrate the capacity to deliver gender-responsive, disability-inclusive, safeguarding-sensitive, and trauma-informed programming, including appropriate referral pathways and accessible and confidential grievance redress mechanisms. (iii) The firm must demonstrate on-the-ground presence, qualified staffing, established networks, and adequate logistical and operational capacity in Kakuma/Kalobeyei and/or Dadaab, including demonstrated ability to mobilize, engage, train, mentor, and provide ongoing support to refugee youth. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

 

 

  1. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulation for IPF Borrowers” dated July 2016 and Revised Fifth Edition September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”) setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOL)

INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION-OPEN INTERNATIONAL

COUNTRY: Zambia

NAME OF PROJECT: Transport Corridors for Economic Resilience (TRACER)

CREDIT NO.: IDA-E2930

ASSIGNMENT TITLE: TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE TO ASSESS THE APPLICATION OF OPEN ACCESS AGREEMENTS ON ZAMBIAN RAILWAYS

REFERENCE NO. ZM-MTOL-458682-CS-INDV

The Government of the Republic of Zambia through the Ministry of Transport and Logistics, has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Transport Corridors for Economic Resilience Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for Individual Consulting Services to undertake a comprehensive assessment of the current Open Access policies and develop a framework for signing Open Access Agreement and model for computation of access fees on Zambia Railways network.

The consulting services will be undertaken in Six (6) months. The individual consultant is expected to review existing policy, legal and frameworks governing rail open access in Zambia; review the current freight open access procedures and requirements in Zambia, conduct research on best international freight open access systems, define gaps and recommend the best approach for Zambia; review the current rail passenger service practices and requirements, conduct research on international passenger open access systems and recommend the best approach for Zambia; review the current Rail Open Access Contracts, develop a standard template and recommend mandatory provisions for inclusion based on international best practices; review the current approaches for charging open access fees compared to other international best practices; and develop a standard model for determination of access fees for all access operators.

The Ministry of Transport and Logistics now invites eligible Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the Consultancy Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services including updated Curriculum Vitae (CV) and a short expression of interest summarizing their understanding and approach of the assignment. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2023 setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

data.project_name: Agriculture Modernization Project
data.institution: International Centre for Food and Agriculture Strategic Development and Research under the Ministry of Agriculture of th
data.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

 

Republic of Uzbekistan

Agriculture Modernization Project

Credit No.: 6549-UZ

 

Assignment Title: International Sector Consultant: Agricultural Financial Markets and Farm Credit Technical Support for the Functional Reform of the State Fund for Agricultural Support

Reference No: AMP/C1/IC/74

The Republic of Uzbekistan has received financing from the World Bank to cover the costs of the Agriculture Modernization Project and intends to use part of the funds for consulting services.

 

The objective of this assignment is to provide technical and strategic support to the Ministry of Economy and Finance in assessing and redesigning the role of the State Fund for Agricultural Support by:

       conducting a comprehensive assessment of the Fund's existing functions, mandate, and institutional arrangements, as well as an evaluation of proposed reforms and transformation options;

       reviewing the agricultural financial market development and effectiveness of farm credit systems in Uzbekistan;

       identifying opportunities to strengthen agricultural finance through market-oriented and risk-based approaches;

       proposing institutional, operational, and financial reforms for the Fund; and

       recommending mechanisms to increase private sector participation and improve access to agricultural finance.

 

The International Consultant Qualifications and Experience:

Education

  • Advanced university degree (Master's or higher) in agricultural economics, finance and financial administration, public policy, or a relevant field.

Experience

  • Minimum 15 years of professional experience in agricultural and rural finance, agricultural financial markets, or agricultural development policy;
  • Demonstrated international experience in the design and implementation of agricultural support reforms and institutional transformations;
  • Proven experience in conducting functional assessments and institutional reviews of public financial sector entities or development finance institutions;
  • Extensive experience in agricultural credit systems, farm finance, risk management, and financial sector development;
  • Experience working with governments, international financial institutions, and development partners in transition or developing economies; and
  • Previous experience in Central Asia or countries with similar agricultural and institutional characteristics will be an advantage.

Skills

  • Excellent understanding of farm finance and credit systems;
  • Strong analytical and strategic advisory skills;
  • Ability to design institutional and functional transformation frameworks and practical implementation roadmaps;
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and facilitation skills; and
  • Fluency in either English or Russian is required. Knowledge of Uzbek would be an asset.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.   

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the IC method set out in the Procurement Regulations.,

 

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours, from 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m.

Expressions of interest (e-mail is acceptable) should be submitted to the address below no later than 6:00 p.m. on 4th September 2026.

 

International Strategic Center for Agri-Food Development under the Ministry of Agriculture of the Republic of Uzbekistan (ISCAD)

Address: Labzak 1-A, 100128, Tashkent, Uzbekistan

Tel: +998 78 555 74 47

E-mail: amp@iscad.uz
