SOLICITAÇÃO DE MANIFESTAÇÃO DE INTERESSE

SERVIÇOS DE CONSULTORIA

BRASIL – Ministério do Meio Ambiente e Mudança do Clima - MMA

Paisagens Sustentáveis da Amazônia - ASL BRASIL 2

Acordo de Doação N.º TF0B6898-BR – Banco Mundial

Número de Referência: BR-FGV-561336-CS-CQS

DE-ASL2-POA3-SEMAS-2026-0001

 

 

Escopo: Seleção e contratação de consultoria não individual (pessoa jurídica) especializada em mapeamento e definição de áreas prioritárias nos Territórios Quilombolas (TQ) Murumuru e TQ Murumurutuba, visando a implementação de um sistema de monitoramento participativo da regeneração da vegetação natural, no âmbito do Projeto Paisagens Sustentáveis da Amazônia (ASL Brasil – Fase 2).

 

O Beneficiário recebeu uma doação do Banco Mundial para a execução do Projeto PAISAGENS SUSTENTÁVEIS DA AMAZÔNIA FASE 2 – ASL BRASIL 2 de n° TF0B6898. O Projeto tem como principal objetivo promover a gestão integrada da paisagem e a conservação de ecossistemas terrestres e de água doce em áreas específicas, a fim de melhorar o manejo e a conectividade de Áreas Protegidas na Região Amazônica.

 

Solicitação de Manifestação de Interesse – SMI Nº 0015/2026

 

A FUNDAÇÃO GETULIO VARGAS, OU SIMPLESMENTE FGV, TORNA PÚBLICO QUE ESTÁ ABERTO O PRAZO PARA CONSULTORIAS ELEGÍVEIS INTERESSADAS NA APRESENTAÇÃO DE MANIFESTAÇÃO DE INTERESSE, COM VISTAS À CONTRATAÇÃO DE CONSULTORIA NÃO INDIVIDUAL (PESSOA JURÍDICA) ESPECIALIZADA EM MAPEAMENTO E DEFINIÇÃO DE ÁREAS PRIORITÁRIAS NOS Territórios Quilombolas (TQ) Murumuru e TQ Murumurutuba, no município de Santarém, estado do Pará, visando subsidiar a implementação de um sistema de monitoramento participativo da regeneração da vegetação natural. As consultorias interessadas deverão demonstrar que são qualificadas e que têm a experiência para desempenhar o serviço, conforme descrito no Termo de Referência, disponível em: https://asl-brasil.fgv.br/compras-e-contratacoes

 

Qualificação Requerida da Consultoria

A consultoria deverá apresentar experiência em:

i.     Execução de, no mínimo, 3 (três) trabalhos concluídos nos últimos 10 (dez) anos, relacionados aos seguintes temas: identificação e mapeamento de áreas com aptidão para restauração florestal ou para regeneração da vegetação natural preferencialmente na Amazônia; implantação, fortalecimento e monitoramento de sistemas produtivos, sistemas agroflorestais, restauração de florestal, agricultura regenerativa, monitoramento da restauração na preferencialmente na Amazônia, mapeamento participativo em territórios quilombolas e outras comunidades tradicionais.

ii.     Execução de, no mínimo, 5 (cinco) contratos, projetos ou serviçosno desenvolvimento de, diagnósticos socioeconômicos e ambientais, desenvolvimento de sistemas agroflorestais, agricultura regenerativa, regeneração da vegetação nativa preferencialmente no estado do Pará e/ou em outras áreas com reconhecimento de gestão integrada na Amazônia.

iii.    Execução de, no mínimo, 3 (três) contratos, projetos ou serviços  de gestão ambiental e territorial com mapeamento participativo em áreas rurais de comunidades agricultoras, extrativistas, quilombolas ou indígenas, preferencialmente na Amazônia.

iv.   Execução de, no mínimo, 3 (três) contratos, projetos ou serviços de planejamento e monitoramento de políticas públicas socioambientais com elaboração de bases de dados, indicadores e sistemas de monitoramento da regeneração da vegetação, preferencialmente na Amazônia.

 

Será considerada diferencial a experiência comprovada na Amazônia Legal e, especialmente, no estado do Pará. A consultoria deverá demonstrar capacidade técnica para planejar e executar pesquisas de campo em múltiplos territórios; produzir análises socioeconômicas, ambientais e institucionais; operar ferramentas de georreferenciamento e sistemas de informação geográfica (SIG); elaborar bancos de dados e indicadores de monitoramento e produzir relatórios técnicos, mapas temáticos e documentos analíticos.

 

A equipe chave deverá contar com os seguintes profissionais:  1 Coordenador(a)-Geral e 1 Especialista em Gestão Territorial e Ambiental . A consultoria deverá designar equipe de apoio necessária para realização das atividades desse TDR, sendo sugerida a inclusão de um técnico para atuar em campo.

 

            As Manifestações de Interesse deverão ser enviadas até dia 10/09/2026, às 23:59 horas, para o e-mail  asl2.compras@fgv.br. As Manifestações deverão estar identificadas como SMI Nº 0015/2026 – Mapeamento TQ Murumuru e Murumurutuba. A consultoria interessada deverá demonstrar capacidade técnica para atuar nos Territórios Quilombolas (TQ) Murumuru e TQ Murumurutuba, no município de Santarém/PA, garantindo que as atividades ocorram conforme o planejamento, que engloba o levantamento participativo de dados territoriais, o mapeamento e a priorização de áreas para regeneração da vegetação natural, e a proposição de um sistema de monitoramento participativo. A consultoria interessada deverá apresentar seu portfólio, os currículos da equipe-chave e demais documentos de acordo com os requisitos definidos no Termo de Referência.

 

Esta Solicitação de Manifestação de Interesse não pressupõe qualquer compromisso de contratação. As consultorias elegíveis serão avaliadas de acordo com as normas do "Regulamento de Aquisições para Mutuários de Operações de Financiamento de Projetos de Investimento, edição de setembro de 2023".

 

Informações adicionais sobre o processo seletivo poderão ser solicitadas pelo endereço eletrônico asl2.compras@fgv.br bb

 

A Fundação Getúlio Vargas entrará em contato somente com as consultorias elegíveis para a próxima etapa do processo.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL SELECTION)

 

Country – Commonwealth of Dominica

 

Assignment Title: Revision of the Waitukubuli Trail Management Plan

Reference No DM-MOERMKU-563329-CS-INDV

Project: Leveraging Eco-Tourism for Biodiversity Protection in Dominica (P170846)

Grant No. TF-B9551

Implementing Agency: Ministry of Environment, Rural Modernisation, Kalinago Upliftment and Constituency Empowerment

1. Background

The Government of the Commonwealth of Dominica has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of Leveraging Eco-Tourism for Biodiversity Protection in Dominica and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The Ministry of Environment, Rural Modernisation, Kalinago Upliftment and Constituency Empowerment intend to procure individual consulting service to revise/develop the Waitukubuli Trail Management Plan.

2. Objective of Assignment

The objective of the assignment is to develop the Waitukubuli National Trail Management Plan, in a highly participatory manner and following best practices worldwide. The result will be an improved management framework and it will provide sustainable trail guidelines for operational aspects of trail management to include conservation, maintenance, utilization, financing, promotion, safety, etc.

3. Required Qualifications & Experience

Qualifications

  • University degree (bachelor's or higher) or equivalent professional qualification in Natural Resource Management, Forestry, Ecology, Eco-tourism, Protected Areas planning and management.

Experience

  • At least 7 years of professional experience in natural resources management.
  • At least 3 similar projects or assignments.
  • Demonstrated experience working with national governments, communities, and diverse stakeholder groups.
  • Demonstrated experience in conducting beneficiary consultations, and stakeholder engagement/participation.
  • Experience in developing planning and management documents and analysis for long-distance trails is an asset.
  • Experience working within Small Developing Island States (SIDS) context would be an asset.
  • Fluency in English with the ability to write in a clear and concise manner. Dominican Creole will be an asset.

Skills

  • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills.
  • Ability to meet deadlines and prioritize multiple tasks.
  • The ability to communicate complex procedures among various stakeholders.
  • Proficiency in the use of Microsoft Office Applications and software.
  • Attention to detail.

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment may be requested by contacting the following email addresses: letbp@dominica.gov.dm or letbpprocurement@gmail.com

4. Submission Requirements

Expressions of Interest shall include:

  1. Letter of interest
  2. Curriculum Vitae
  3. Description of Similar assignment
  4. Details of experience working with national governments, communities, and diverse stakeholder groups.
  5. Details of experience in conducting beneficiary consultations, and stakeholder engagement/participation.

 

EOI’s should be a max of 5-10 pages.

Expressions of interest must be submitted in a written form (in person, or by mail, or by e-mail) to the following addresses:

 

Attn: Project Coordinator

Leveraging Eco-Tourism for Biodiversity Protection in

      Dominica Project

First Floor, 38 Cork Street

Roseau, Commonwealth of Dominica

E-mail: letbp@dominica.gov.dm letbpprocurement@gmail.com copied to letpb.procurement@gmail.com .

 

Deadline for Submission: 4:00 p.m. Eastern Caribbean Time (ECT), September 10, 2026

Further information can be obtained through letbp@dominica.gov.dm or letbpprocurement@gmail.com to seek clarification.

5. Shortlisting and Selection

In the assessment of submissions, consideration will be given to the applicant’s qualifications, relevant professional experience, and experience in similar assignments, including experience in participatory stakeholder engagement and the development of management plans for long-distance trails. Only experience clearly demonstrated and supported by the submitted documentation will be considered. The Individual Consultant who is determined to be the best qualified and experienced for the assignment will be selected.

6. Fraud and Corruption

The attention of interested Individuals is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” 7th Edition (September 2025) setting forth the World Bank’s policy on Conflict of Interest.  In addition, please refer to the following specific information on conflict of interest related to this assignment i.e., 3.17 (c) & (d) of the Procurement Regulation.

Assignment Title: Consultancy for the Development of a City-Wide Inclusive Sanitation (CWIS) Plan for Freetown City Council (FCC) and Western Area Rural District Council (WARD-C)

Reference No: SL-MWRS-539782-CS-QCBS

The Government of Sierra Leone, through the Ministry of Water Resources and Sanitation, has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Sierra Leone Water Security and WASH Access Improvement Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Service”) is to develop comprehensive City-Wide Inclusive Sanitation (CWIS) Implementation Plans for FCC and WARD-C aimed to achieve equitable, safe, and sustainable sanitation services for all.

The assignment is expected to commence in or around January 2026. The total duration of the assignment is expected to be 36 weeks from the date of contract signing.

The detailed Terms of Reference can  be obtained electronically upon request from the email addresses stated below :  queed10928@gmail.com , ingamara20131@gmail.com ,  Cc kawenikargbo7@gmail.com , gibriljabba@hotmail.com or in paper form at the address : The Project Coordinator , Ministry of Water Resource and Sanitation , 56 Liverpool Street, Freetown, Sierra Leone.

The Ministry of Water Resources and Sanitation, the implementing entity responsible for this assignment, invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The shortlisting criteria are:

  1. Core business and years of experience (how it is relevant to the assignment);
  2. Number of years in business, both as a registered business entity and in providing services in the sector(s) that are relevant to this assignment;
  3. Management structure, number of directors and total number of staff – full time, on contract and as associates (however, Key Personnel and their specific experiences are not evaluated at this stage);
  4. Financial performance (e.g. turnover and profitability) in the last three years;
  5. Enlist firm’s experience. For each similar assignment undertaken by the firm, it is required to state the cost, whether it undertook the job solely, in partnership with other firms (name them and the role of your firm), and name of the client, the duration of the assignment, the number of staff/person-day(s) your firm engaged on the assignment, cost of the assignment (and cost of the project, if available), status of completeness as at time of expression of interest for this assignment, a brief scope of work for the assignment, etc.
  6. Regional and comparable-country experience

d. Household, institutional and commercial demand assessment, including affordability and consumer behaviour.

e. Financing, investment and carbon finance assessment.

f. Environmental, climate, health, gender and social inclusion assessment.

ASSIGNMENT TITLE:            CONSULTING SERVICES TO DEVELOP FEASIBILITY STUDIES FOR MONGOLIAN CIVIL AVIATION SECTOR AND MURUN (4C AERODROME CODE) AIRPORT IMPROVEMENT PROJECT

REFERENCE NO.

(AS PER PROCUREMENT PLAN):              ZTYA/20260804058

The Government of Mongolia has received a grant financing from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD), through the Global Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP) toward the cost of the Gobi Connectivity Improvement Project under Grant No. TF0D0692 and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.  

The consulting services (“the Services”) include two distinct but complementary components.

Component A will establish the analytical and strategic foundations for aviation sector development in Mongolia. It will include a comprehensive aviation sector diagnostic, a proportionate first-pass review of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) safety and security compliance issues relevant to airport network planning and investment readiness, preparation of the Mongolia Airport Network Development Strategy to 2040, a companion Policy Recommendations Note, and a structured stakeholder consultation process. Together, these outputs will provide Government with a practical framework for airport classification, demand development, institutional strengthening, climate resilience, high-level investment prioritization, and identification of follow-on policy and technical assistance needs.

Component B will prepare a full feasibility study for Murun Airport. The Government has identified Murun Airport as a priority project requiring detailed assessment and project preparation. The feasibility study shall evaluate the technical, operational, environmental, social, financial, economic, fiscal, and institutional viability of the proposed investment and define an appropriate development concept for implementation.

The assignment is expected to run for approximately 6 to 7 months from the date of contract effectiveness. Component A and Component B shall proceed in parallel throughout the assignment period.

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the primary procurement stage for the assignment can be found at the following website:

Tender.gov.mn

General experience implementing consultancy services in the field of civil aviation and transport sector strategy, planning and the feasibility studies; and preliminary/detailed engineering design of projects in cold climate regions, including economic/financial analysis and safeguard integration, during the last 10 years;

Evidence should be provided in the firm`s EoI.

  1. Specific Experiences:

Proven experience in preparing civil aviation sector development strategies and/or airport feasibility studies (including associated policy, institutional, or PPP/commercial advisory) during the last 10 years. At least 2 such similar contracts should be demonstrated, each with a contract value of not less than US$300,000 (Please be sure to include the contract value in your submission).
  2. The consulting team must include Environmental and Social Specialists with demonstrated experience applying the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) or equivalent international safeguard/environmental and social risk management standards. At minimum, the team must demonstrate capacity to address environmental screening, social impact assessment, resettlement risk assessment, stakeholder engagement, and GBV/SEA/SH risk management.

General description of the firm's technical and managerial organization, including the structure of the organization, general qualifications of staff, and number of permanent professional staff. Do not provide CVs of key staff. Key experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

AVIS À MANIFESTATION D'INTÉRÊT

« SÉLECTION D’UN CONSULTANT INDIVIDUEL NATIONAL POUR L’ÉVALUATION DES POINTS D’ENTRÉE (PoE) ET DES CENTRES DE SURVEILLANCE ÉPIDÉMIOLOGIQUE (CSE) »

 

  1. Contexte

 Le Gouvernement de la République du Tchad, à travers le Ministère de la Santé Publique et de la Prévention, bénéficie de l’appui financier de la Banque mondiale pour la mise en œuvre du Projet [nom du Projet].

Dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre des activités du Projet, il est prévu de renforcer les capacités nationales de prévention, de détection et de réponse aux menaces sanitaires, notamment à travers l’amélioration des capacités de surveillance épidémiologique et des capacités requises au niveau des Points d’Entrée (PoE), conformément aux exigences du Règlement sanitaire international (RSI, 2005).

À cet effet, le Projet envisage de recruter un Consultant Individuel National chargé de réaliser une évaluation exhaustive des capacités des Points d’Entrée (PoE) et des Centres de Surveillance Épidémiologique (CSE).

  1. Objet de la mission

La mission consiste à réaliser une évaluation détaillée et documentée des capacités de l’ensemble des Points d’Entrée (PoE) et des Centres de Surveillance Épidémiologique (CSE) concernés, afin d’identifier les capacités existantes, les insuffisances, les écarts par rapport aux exigences applicables, ainsi que les besoins prioritaires de renforcement.

Le consultant devra notamment effectuer des visites physiques sur l’ensemble des sites concernés et produire un rapport d’évaluation assorti d’un plan d’amélioration opérationnel et priorisé.

  1. Profil et qualifications requis

Le consultant devra notamment répondre aux exigences suivantes :

  • être titulaire au minimum d’un Master en santé publique, épidémiologie, médecine, santé internationale ou dans un domaine directement pertinent ;
  • justifier d’au moins cinq (5) années d’expérience professionnelle pertinente dans les systèmes de surveillance épidémiologique ;
  • disposer d’une expérience avérée dans l’évaluation des systèmes de surveillance et/ou des systèmes de santé ;
  • disposer d’une expérience dans l’évaluation des capacités sanitaires des Points d’Entrée (PoE) ;
  • avoir une excellente connaissance du RSI (2005) ;
  • avoir une bonne maîtrise de la Surveillance Intégrée de la Maladie et la Riposte (SIMR) ;
  • disposer d’une expérience dans la préparation et la réponse aux urgences de santé publique ;
  • avoir une bonne capacité de collecte, de traitement et d’analyse des données ;
  • disposer d’excellentes capacités rédactionnelles et analytiques en français ;
  • maîtriser les outils bureautiques et les outils d’analyse et de traitement des données ;
  • avoir une bonne connaissance du contexte du système de santé et du dispositif national de surveillance épidémiologique du Tchad.
  • Une expérience de travail avec le Ministère de la Santé Publique et de la Prévention et/ou les structures nationales de surveillance constituera un avantage.
  1. Durée de la mission

La durée prévisionnelle de la mission est de quatre-vingt-dix (90) jours calendaires.

La mission nécessitera des déplacements à N’Djaména ainsi que dans les provinces et localités où sont implantés les PoE et les CSE concernés par l’évaluation.

5. Méthode de sélection

Le consultant sera recruté conformément aux dispositions du Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant un Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) de la Banque mondiale, édition septembre 2025, selon la méthode de Sélection de Consultants Individuels (CI).

5. Dépôt des manifestations d’intérêt

data.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – CONSULTANCY FIRM)

ALBANIA

Project: National Water Supply and Sanitation Sector Modernization Program (P4R)

TF No.: B8448

Assignment Title: Strategic Coastal Water Supply Framework and Feasibility Studies for Priority Water Supply Investments in the South Coast of Albania

Reference No.: AL-AKUK -329330-CS-QCBS

Albania is implementing governance and service reforms in the WSS sector supported by the World Bank through P4R project financed by SECO (Swiss Government). In parallel, structural reform changes are being launched by the government, including the creation of the new Water Production Operator (OPU) while the details of its future role and structure are still evolving; therefore this assignment shall focus on AKUK’s current mandate and existing institutional set-up, and reflect OPU-related interfaces only where and when formally clarified or necessary as working assumptions.

 

This Request for Expressions of Interest aims to assist AKUK in hiring a Consultant to prepare a Feasibility Study for potable water supply within the defined Project Area with a planning horizon extending to 2050, building upon the analyses, methodologies and strategic planning principles developed under the DWD DSIP and subsequent sector planning initiatives.

The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: https://akuk.gov.al/

The activities described in these TORs are expected to be completed within a period of 10 months, following the signing of the consultancy contract.

The consulting firm shall demonstrate proven experience in assignments of similar nature, including:

  • At least one (1) completed projects in strategic water supply planning, master planning, or system development studies;
  • At least one (1) assignments involving water resources assessment and supply-demand balance analysis;
  • At least one (1) projects including water demand forecasting based on demographic, tourism, and consumption scenarios;
  • At least one (1) assignment involving strategic assessment of water supply infrastructure alternatives;
  • At least one (1) project including economic and technical evaluation of alternatives;
  • At least one (1) project carried out for a water utility, public water operator, or public authority responsible for water services;
  • Experience in GIS-based infrastructure planning and spatial analysis.
  • Experience in projects implemented in tourism-intensive areas or comparable environments will be considered an asset.
  • Preference will be given to firms with experience in projects financed by International Financial Institutions (IFI) or European Union programmes.

The assignment shall be carried out by a multidisciplinary team. The indicative total input is of approximately sixty-five (65) person-months, reflecting the feasibility, environmental and social, and field investigation components. The core team shall include, at minimum:

  • Team Leader / Senior Water Supply Engineer;
  • Water Resources / Hydrogeologist;
  • Hydraulic Modelling Engineer;
  • Financial/Economic Analyst;
  • Environmental Specialist (P-ESIA);
  • Social Development Specialist (ESS5/ESS10);
  • GIS and Data Management Specialist;
  • Institutional/Utility Specialist;
  • Climate Resilience Specialist,

The proposed experts may be national and/or international, as appropriate for the assignment, and supported by additional experts, survey teams and field investigation activities. The Consultant shall justify the proposed allocation of expert inputs in its Technical Proposal. Please see criteria for the experts within ToRs document.

The evaluation criteria to be used for selecting the successful Consultant will be the following:

•           General Qualifications, including core business and years in business, (30 points);

•           Relevant experience, including previous experience in the field of assignment, (70 points);

The service will be selected under the provisions of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (Procurement Regulations), in investment project financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services November 2020, in accordance with Quality and Cost Based Selecton (QCBS), Lump-Sum Contract. The Bank requires that firms or individuals involved in Bank IPF procurement shall not have conflict of interest.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 08:00 to 16:00, Mondays to Thursdays, and from 08:00 to 14:00 on Fridays.

data.notice_text:
NATIONAL LOCAL GOVERNMENT FINANCE COMMITTEE

                      Governance to Enable Service Delivery (GESD) Project – GESD 2.0

                                                  Agreement No:  IDA-E6540

Individual Consultant- Project Engineer (2)

No: MW-NLGFC-563895-CS-INDIV/ MW-NLGFC-563897-CS-INDIV

                     

                                          Date of Issue: 20th August ,2026

  1. Background

 

The Government of Malawi (GoM) through the National Local Government Finance Committee (NLGFC) has received financing towards the cost of Governance to Enable Service Delivery (GESD) Project. The NLGFC intends to apply part of the proceeds of this financing to eligible payments under the contract for hiring two Project Engineer on a three - year contract renewable annually based on performance and availability of financial resources or mutually agreed by both parties.    

 

NLGFC therefore invites applications from suitably qualified and interested candidates to fill the position of two (2) Project Engineer tenable at the NLGFC Offices. The terms of Reference (TORs) for two (2) Project Engineer) are as follows:

 

2. The Objectives of the Assignment

The Project Engineer (Specialist) shall lead, coordinate and support local authorities and all relevant ministries, departments and agencies in the design and implementation of the project. The Project Engineer (Specialist) will lead and have approving authority for preparing and/or interpreting designs, bill of quantities (BoQs), tendering and engineering cost estimates prepared. The Project Engineer (Specialist) will work closely with relevant district authorities, including district engineers, other officers and specialists in the PIT, including safeguards, Project Coordinator, NLGFC, MoLGRD and other relevant stakeholders, including but not limited to supervision consultants. The Project Engineer (Specialist) will support monitoring of the sub-projects and will address and manage technical engineering questions in local investment projects implemented by the local authorities that are financed by GESD 2.0. 

 

  1. Duties and Responsibilities of the Project Engineer (Consultant)

 

The Project Engineers (Consultants) will be responsible for providing technical leadership and engineering oversight to ensure that project activities are planned, designed, implemented, monitored, and completed in accordance with approved specifications, quality standards, budget, schedule, and applicable regulations.

 

Specific tasks will include the following:

 

  1. Coordinate and support all engineering functions and activities related to infrastructure construction and rehabilitation in the local authorities, namely Department of Planning and Development and Department of Public Works;
  2. Support data collection for all proposed sub-project sites to aid development and customisation of architectural designs, production of BoQs and engineering estimates, tendering processes and ensuring that designs are in conformity with results of site-specific resilience and risk related investigations and analysis;
  3. Ensure timely and correct submission of information into the Public Management Information System (PMIS) by local authorities;
  4. Provide technical support to the Local Authorities in project selection, reviewing annual investment plans, works designs, BoQs, costs estimate, tendering, supervision and monitoring;
  5. Coordinate topographic surveys for the design of infrastructure to be developed under the Project;
  6. Support local authorities in conducting initial site investigation;
  7. Facilitate the production of location maps and sketches if necessary for all engineering sites that need maintenance and repair (selected as subprojects under GESD 2.0);
  8. Support and if necessary lead the review and approval of submissions by design engineers, including ensuring timely submission of the same;
  9. Support and if necessary lead design options stakeholder consultations with communities and relevant departments so that their inputs are incorporated in the designs to ensure acceptance and ownership of solutions to be developed;
  10. Conduct technical supervision of all construction works ensuring that the works are implemented to the required standards, within the assigned cost and time;
  11. Check Supervision Consultant’s work so as to conduct verification of contractors’ payment claims for works done;
  12. Manage changes to engineering constructions works ensuring that any changes have no adverse effect on the project and they are undertaken following project works change protocols, including documentation;
  13. Facilitate preparation of work plans and budgets for local investment projects to ensure relevance to outputs and outcomes of local investment project;
  14. Support the preparation of schedule of works and materials for project activities in collaboration with relevant stakeholders;
  15. Review and assess contractors’ and consultants’ payment certificates for engineering works
  16. Prepare and conduct training programs for Local Authority technical staff involved in contract and procurement management; and other related activities as directed by the PIT;
  17. Ensure compliance with all statutory and regulatory requirements;
  18. Liaise with other project specialists and officers, including safeguards, occupational health & safety, procurement, and advise the PIT on all construction Engineering technical related matters;
  19. Collect projects’ progress reports from the LAs, liaise with the monitoring & evaluation officer in the PIT in producing reports for project activities, consolidate them and submit them to PIT/PC, Executive Director and World Bank Task Team;
  20. Preparation and timely submission of monthly, quarterly and annual engineering project progress reports and other reports to the Project Coordinator, Executive Director and the World Bank Task Team.
  21. Facilitating the review of Annual Investment Plans (AIPs) for Local authorities and provide guidance on cost and time estimates.

 

  1. Deliverables

 

Deliverables for the assignment correspond to the duties and responsibilities above. Specifically, they will comprise:

 

  1. Timely review of AIPs submitted by local authorities, including review of cost and time estimates;
  2. Reviewed and approved engineering designs and drawings.
  3. Technical specifications and BoQs.
  4. Engineering project progress reports and other reports timely compiled
  5. Site inspection reports.
  6. Quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC) reports.
  7. Defects and corrective action reports.
  8. Monthly and quarterly progress reports, aligned with PMIS information.
  9. Physical progress monitoring reports.
  10. Work completion certificates.

 

  1. Performance Criteria

 

The following performance criteria will be used to assess the performance of the Project Engineer annually and based upon these assessments the contract with the project (GESD 2.0) may be continued or terminated:

  • 100% of required technical reports submitted on time.
  • At least 95% compliance with approved engineering specifications and quality standards.
  • Site inspections conducted according to approved supervision schedules.
  • 100% of contractor payment certificates reviewed and processed within agreed timelines.
  • All identified defects and non-compliance issues addressed within specified corrective action periods.
  • Minimal cost and schedule overruns attributable to technical deficiencies.
  • No major engineering failures or quality-related incidents.
  • Timely completion and handover of project infrastructure.
  • PMIS utilization by local authorities.

 

  1. Qualifications, Skills and Expertise

 

The candidate should meet the following minimum qualifications:

 

  1. Bachelor’s Degree in Civil Engineering/Architecture/Quantity Surveying
  2. Master’s Degree in Construction/Engineering related field and ;
  3. Registration with an approved professional body, such as Malawi Engineering Institution/Board of Architects and Quantity Surveyors
  4. A minimum of 8 years of relevant working experience;
  5. Excellent communications, writing/reporting skills;
  6. Proficiency in computer aided design packages (AutoCAD, ArchCAD, GIS etc)
  7. Proficient in the use of Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Microsoft Project etc.);
  8. Strong organizational, self-starting and communications skills;
  9. Experience working with government institutions and organizations; working experience with local authorities in Malawi is considered an advantage;
  10. Highly motivated and enthusiastic person with excellent planning, analytical, communications and interpersonal skills as well as a high level of diplomacy; and
  11. Excellent oral and written communication skills in English, as well as team participation and management skills

 

  1. Reporting Arrangements

 

The Project Engineer (Specialist) will primarily report to the Project Coordinator with a technical reporting line to the Director of Social and Economic Services at NLGFC for all technical matters, and will support local authorities’ in implementation of GESD 2.0 project.

 

  1. Location of Assignment

 

The Project Engineer (Specialist) will be based at the NLGFC offices in Lilongwe. The Project Engineer (Consultant) will occasionally be required to travel to local government authorities in Malawi where the Project is implementing its activities to engage with district officials to guide and improve project implementation.

 

  1. Duration of Assignment

 

The assignment is expected to span a total period of up to three (3) years, with annual performance reviews and contract extensions subject to satisfactory performance.

.

8.MODE OF APPLICATION

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14. 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations of IPF Borrowers” dated September, 2025 (“Procurement regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest and A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant (INDV) selection method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

Further information including the detailed Terms of Reference (TORs) can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 7:30 hours to 12:00 hours and from 13:00 hours to 16:30 hours except on Weekends and Public Holidays

 

9. SUBMISSION OF APPLICATIONS

Interested applicants who meet the above requirements should submit application letters together with concise Curriculum Vitae (CV), National ID, and copies of relevant certificates to the address below not later than 17.30 hours on Friday, 11th September 2026.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

 

Country

:

Indonesia

Name of Project

:

Indonesia Health Systems Strengthening (IHSS) Project

Loan No.

:

IBRD Loan No. 9626

Assignment Title:

:

Commercial Compliance and Documentation Assurance Consultancy Firm

Reference No.

:

ID-COMP 4 IHSS-550312-CS-QCBS

 

  1. The Ministry of Health (MoH) of the Republic of Indonesia has received loan financing from the World Bank to support the implementation of the Indonesia Health System Strengthening (IHSS) Project, with total funding amounting to EUR 3.7 billion. The IHSS Project operates at an unprecedented scale, serving over 10,000 health facilities across Indonesia's 6,500 inhabited islands, involving high-volume and complex procurement of medical and laboratory equipment. Given this complexity, MoH requires additional capacity to strengthen its commercial documentation, compliance arrangements, and governance processes. To address this, MoH intends to engage a suitably qualified consulting firm to provide concurrent commercial compliance advisory and review support. The selected firm will work in close coordination with the Inspectorate General (IG), the probity auditor, and the World Bank to ensure alignment and avoid duplication of efforts.
  2. The consulting services ("the Services") consist of concurrent commercial compliance audit and advisory support to MoH for the implementation of the IHSS Project, with a focus on transactions, engagements, and communications with vendors, suppliers, and other private sector actors across the SOPHI, SIHREN, InPULS, and project management components. The scope of services will include, but not be limited to, the following: (1) commercial compliance reviews of vendor engagements and procurement transactions; (2) design and implementation of a commercial documentation and indexing framework; (3) risk identification and mitigation in commercial practices; (4) preparation of a Commercial Compliance Whitepaper; and (5) capacity building and training for MoH staff.  
  3. The assignment is expected to require approximately 120 professional staff-months over the implementation period. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: https://s.kemkes.go.id/CCDAConsultancyFirm 
  4. The Services for Commercial Compliance and Documentation Assurance Consultancy Firm is expected to commence in November 2026 and conclude by April 2028.
  5. The Ministry of Health (MoH) now invites eligible firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide sufficient information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services (including the name and location/country of the Client, type and scope of services provided, period of contract, contract amount, role of the firm, starting and completion dates, key output delivered and experts involved in the assignment). The shortlisting criteria are:
  • Legal Status and Registration: The firm must be a legally registered entity with a valid business license, and possess national and/or international accreditations/registrations (e.g., ISO 37001, ISO 9001, or equivalent certification).
  • Core Business and Years in Business: Minimum ten (10) years of proven experience in any of the following core business areas: commercial auditing, compliance review, and probity assurance. Other line of business such as strategic advisory related to procurement, contracting, and risk management will be considered as an advantage.
  • Relevant Project Experience:
    • Successfully implemented at least three (3) similar assignments within the last seven (7) years, demonstrating experience in any of the following areas:
      • commercial compliance audits or reviews in the public sector or health services; 
      • development of compliance frameworks or governance-oriented whitepapers; 
      • strategic advisory support in procurement and contracting processes; 
      • relevant project experience should be similar in nature, complexity, and scale to the current assignment, including key components such as commercial compliance review, procurement advisory, and risk assessment. 
      •  
      • Similar experience in any of the above areas under projects financed by Multilateral Development Banks (MDBs) such as the World Bank, ADB, AIIB, and IsDB, is an advantage.
    • Experience in establishing knowledge management systems, databases, and tested methodologies to support the implementation of nationwide projects is an advantage.
  • Technical and Managerial Capability of the Firm: Availability of a qualified team of multidisciplinary experts with demonstrated competencies in law, auditing, risk management, documentation, and information systems. 
  1. The qualifications and experience of Key Experts shall not be included in the shortlisting criteria. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage. The MoH will evaluate the Expressions of Interest (EOI) and develop a shortlist of qualified firms. Shortlisted firms will subsequently be invited to submit full technical and financial proposals in accordance with the World Bank's “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” Fifth Edition September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”).
  2. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” Fifth Edition September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.
  3. The Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but shall clearly indicate in EOI whether the association is in the form of a Joint Venture (JV) and/or a sub-consultancy arrangement. 1.    The Government of Sri Lanka has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Regional Empowerment through Vibrant, Inclusive, and Viable Economies (REVIVE) Project. The Ministry of Transport, Highways and Urban Development (MoTHUD), serving as the Executing Agency, intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

2.    The consulting services (“the Services”) include an integrated sustainability assessment to identify and prioritize environmentally sustainable, socially inclusive, climate-resilient and financially viable tourism and related livelihood investment opportunities in the Jaffna Outer Islands. The Services include biodiversity, environmental, climate and safeguard assessment; socio-economic, cultural and community assessment; market and demand assessment; technical and infrastructure assessment; financial and economic analysis; institutional and governance capacity assessment; sustainable investment planning and prioritization; stakeholder engagement; and preparation of an evidence-based implementation roadmap for future investment planning.

3.    The total duration of the assignment is expected to be twelve (12) months from contract commencement and expected to commence in mid of December 2026.

4.    The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: https://www.transport.gov.lk/ (Urban Development  > Integrated Regional Development Programme).

5.    The Chairman of the Ministry Consultants Procurement Committee, on behalf of the REVIVE Project, now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they possess the required firm-level qualifications, relevant experience and institutional capacity to perform the assignment.

 The shortlisting criteria are as follows:

a.     Legal status, core business and institutional experience: The Consultant shall be a legally registered consulting firm with at least ten (10) years of corporate experience in one or more of the following areas: sustainable tourism and destination development; coastal and marine resource management; biodiversity conservation; socio-economic and livelihood development; financial and economic analysis; and investment planning.

b.     Comparable assignment experience: Successful completion, during the last ten (10) years, of at least three (3) comparable consultancy assignments. A comparable assignment means a master plan, tourism or destination development plan, sustainability assessment, feasibility study, investment plan, or similar strategic planning assignment comparable in nature and multidisciplinary complexity to the present assignment. Collectively, the assignments shall demonstrate experience across several relevant dimensions, including sustainable tourism or destination development, biodiversity and environmental assessment, social and livelihood assessment, climate resilience, infrastructure planning, financial and economic analysis, institutional or governance assessment, stakeholder engagement, and investment prioritization. At least one (1) assignment shall have been undertaken in an island, coastal, remote, environmentally sensitive, or similarly complex geographic setting.

c.     Multidisciplinary institutional capability: Demonstrated institutional capacity to undertake a multidisciplinary sustainability assessment. The Consultant, including any joint venture, shall collectively demonstrate capacity in sustainable tourism and destination development, biodiversity and environmental assessment, social and livelihood assessment, climate resilience, infrastructure planning, financial and economic analysis, and institutional or governance assessment.

d.     Relevant geographic experience: Experience in Sri Lanka, South Asia, or other coastal and island environments with comparable ecological, social and implementation conditions will be considered an advantage during shortlisting.

The Consultant shall provide documentary evidence, such as signed contracts, completion certificates, client references, or equivalent records, to substantiate the firm-level experience claimed.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The Consultant shall provide information demonstrating that they have required qualification and relevant

experience to perform the services and should submit:

i)     Company profiles, qualifications of board of members, brochures, etc.

ii)    List of similar projects completed including foreign funded projects over the last ten years, along with the size of the associate consultancy contracts in man month and US Dollars equivalent terms (with contact details of the client).

iii)   Audited financial statement for last five years.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (July 2016, revised September 2025), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

6.    Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but shall indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all members shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. Please note that a firm / organization is allowed to participate in only one submission as a sole consultant, joint venture partner or a sub –Consultant.

7.    A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (July 2016, revised September 2025).

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

Grant No.: P P514153

Assignment Title: Procurement of Consultancy Services to Develop and Deploy the Africa RISE Gateway

Reference No: 926/AUDA/DITIR/RESILIENTIRRIGATIONF/QCBS/2026

Method: Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS)

 

  1. Introduction

The African Union Development Agency – New Partnership for Africa Development (AUDA-NEPAD) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the “Resilient Irrigation for a Sustainable Economy Project”, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. “Consultancy Services to Develop and Deploy the Africa RISE Gateway”

 

  1. Description of Services

The consulting services (“the Services”) include: Task 1: Africa RISE User Requirements Assessment: Map and profile all user groups and partners including relevant African Union agencies and departments (AUDANEPAD, AU-SAFGRAD, SEBE), government ministries, transboundary water management agencies, regulators, MPA focal points, implementing partners, research institutes and universities and technical experts, farmers, aggregators, private sector, equipment suppliers and financial institutions and farmer unions and cooperative societies etc; Task 2: Design, Develop and Commission the Africa RISE Gateway: Define system architecture, data structures, modules, dashboard requirements and process workflows, including a unified data interoperability Layer that meets vPIC standards and aligns with the Africa RISE Regional Geospatial Analytics Platform and national irrigation monitoring systems.  The architecture shall specify: (a) the endpoints and payload schemas through which national data collection tools, the Regional Geospatial Platform,  and other authorized external data sources submit and validate benchmarking data; (b) the data lineage and version control mechanisms ensuring that published benchmarks are traceable to their submission source; and (c) the traffic-light alert logic that translates performance indicator values into color-coded risk flags for display in the executive dashboard. Task 3: Technical Assistance (TA) and Capacity Building: Develop and deliver a structured, tiered capacity-building programme and associated training materials for all user groups, comprising: (i) a Technical Track for AUDA-NEPAD IT personnel, national technical focal points and system administrators, covering system administration, data management, integration and cybersecurity; (ii) an Operational Track for programme managers, extension officers and policy stakeholders, focusing on effective use of the platform and its functional modules; and (iii) an End-User Track providing simplified guidance and orientation materials. Task 4: Sustainable Operation and Maintenance (O&M) Model for the Gateway: Assess the technical and operational requirements for sustained operation of the Gateway, including hosting, security, data management, updates, user support and maintenance schedules and prepare indicative annual cost projections for the post-project period. Task 5: Envisaged functionality of the Africa RISE Gateway: The Africa RISE Gateway, as a go-to information and knowledge solution, is envisaged to serve.

 

  1. Level of Effort for Key staff:

 

Key Expert

Person-Days

90

75

160

110

55

50

80

Total

620

 

  1. Duration of the assignment

 Total duration: 56 weeks from the date of contract signature

 

  1. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found on the following website: https://www.nepad.org/corporate-procurement#tenders

 

  1. Shortlisting criteria:

The African Union Development Agency – New Partnership for Africa Development (AUDA-NEPAD) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

 

  • The firm shall demonstrate at least ten (10) years of proven institutional experience in designing, developing, deploying and supporting large-scale digital platforms of similar scope and complexity, preferably for regional, public sector or international development programmes.

 

  • The firm should have completed at least three (3) comparable assignments involving enterprise system architecture, API-first platform development, knowledge management systems, data integration, analytics dashboards, workflow management, cloud hosting, cybersecurity, user support and long-term system maintenance.

 

  • Relevant experience should include assignments involving interoperability with existing digital ecosystems, geospatial or remote sensing data integration, benchmarking and performance monitoring dashboards, multilingual knowledge repositories, data governance, user access controls and institutional handover.

 

  • The firm should also demonstrate experience working with government institutions, regional organisations, development partners and multi-country stakeholder groups in Africa, including the delivery of virtual consultations, capacity building, documentation and post-launch technical support.

 

  • Experience in agriculture, irrigation, water management, climate resilience, infrastructure, innovation financing or related sectors will be an added advantage.

 

  • The firm should have evidence of at least 3 assignments of similar nature in the region

 

  1. Conflict of interest

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.15, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” February 2025  (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.  In addition, please refer to the following specific information on conflict of interest related to this assignment:

  1. A firm that has been engaged by the Borrower to provide Goods, Works, or Non-consulting Services for a project (or an affiliate that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with that firm), shall be disqualified from providing Consulting Services resulting from, or directly related to, those Goods, Works, or Non-consulting Services. This provision does not apply to the various firms (Consultants, contractors, or suppliers), which together are performing the contractor’s obligations under a turnkey or design and build contract;

This provision does not apply to the various firms (Consultants, contractors, or suppliers), which together are performing the contractor’s obligations under a turnkey or design and build contract;

Neither a Consultant (including personnel and sub-consultants), nor an affiliate (that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with that Consultant), shall be hired for any assignment that, by its nature, creates a conflict of interest with another assignment of the Consultant;

data.notice_text:
REPUBLIC OF MOZAMBIQUE

MINISTRY OF FINANCE

NATIONAL DIRECTORATE OF STATE ASSETS

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (Individual Consultants)

Assignment title:  e-Government Procurement Senior Expert

 

Reference nr:  MZ-MF-568370-CS-INDV

Loan/Grant Number: IDA-E7400

 

1. The Government of Mozambique, through the Ministry of Finance, is preparing a new governance operation and is currently implementing a Project Preparation Advance (PPA) to support its design. The operation seeks to strengthen public financial management and public procurement as key levers of good governance, transparency, and value for money in the use of public resources.

2. As part of this initiative, the Government intends to apply a portion of the proceeds to the recruitment of consulting services provided by an individual consultant. The consulting services (“the Services”) will include, but are not limited to, the following activities as detailed in the Terms of Reference:

i. Identify overall project risks and develop and maintain a strategy to manage and mitigate them;

ii. Determine project resource requirements and prepare and manage the corresponding budget and work plan;

iii. Ensure the effective management of all contracts related to the project, monitoring performance against agreed obligations and service levels;

iv. Meet all quality-assurance standards applicable to project management and to the e-GP solution;

v. Build and disseminate the requisite knowledge and capability within the Government of Mozambique to support the effective operation of the e-GP system; and

vi. Provide advisory support for an effective and smooth transition from the implementation phase to operation, maintenance, adoption and long-term sustainability of the e-GP system.

3. The e-Government Procurement Senior Expert will be engaged under a time-based contract for an initial period of two (2) years, renewable subject to need and to satisfactory performance, evaluated on an annual basis.

4. The detailed Terms of Reference for the assignment may be obtained at the address below or by email.

5. The attention of interested consultants is drawn to section III, paragraphs 3.15 and 3.16 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (Procurement in Investment Project Financing), Sixth Edition, February 2025, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

6. The Ministry of Finance through the National Directorate of State Assets (DNPE), now invites eligible individual consultants to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services in the form of a curriculum vitae. A consultant will be selected in accordance with the individual consultant selection method set out in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (Procurement in Investment Project Financing), Sixth Edition, February 2025 that can be accessed via the World Bank website at www.world bank.org/ procurement.

7. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to the minimum qualification criteria for the Consultancy are:

i. A Master’s degree in Business Administration, Management, Procurement, Information Technology, Information Systems, Software Engineering or a related discipline.  

ii. At least ten (10) years of relevant professional experience, including a minimum of five (5) years managing information-systems or ICT projects in a public- or private-sector organization;

iii. Demonstrated experience managing large, complex projects, preferably including e-procurement, e-government or comparable digital-transformation initiatives;

iv. Experience in a procurement or procurement-coordination function, and knowledge of public procurement, public-sector operations and change management (a strong advantage);

v. Experience working with projects financed by cooperation partners (e.g. the World Bank, the European Union or the African Development Bank), including familiarity with their procurement and reporting procedures; and

vi. Proficiency in Microsoft Office and relevant project-management tools and software.

vii. Excellent leadership, coordination and stakeholder-management skills;

viii. Ability to manage and prioritize multiple work streams simultaneously and to respond effectively and promptly to sensitive demands and queries;

ix. Strong analytical, problem-solving and decision-making skills; and

x. Excellent written and oral communication skills. Proficiency in Portuguese and a working knowledge of English (or vice versa) is required.

8. Further information may be obtained at the address stated below during office hours, from 7:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m.

9. Expressions of Interest, in the form of a submission letter accompanied by a curriculum vitae, must be delivered in writing to the address below — either in person, by mail, or by email — no later than September 11, 2026, at 3:30 p.m. (local time).

 

Address:                   

Ministry of Finance

449/469, Julius Nyerere Avenue, Bloc A, 11rd floor

Email: procurement.mozprospera@gmail.com  

 Maputo – Mozambique

Estimados señores:

1. El Programa de GESTION RESILIENTE DEL AGUA PARA RIEGO COMUNITARIO Y FAMILIAR a través del P178861 - CONTRATO DE PRÉSTAMO N° 9643-BO, tiene como objetivo la gestión integrada de recursos hídricos con enfoque de cuenca e incrementar la resiliencia ante la variabilidad climática de familias rurales vulnerables en microcuencas seleccionados. Sus objetivos específicos son: i) Apoyar a las familias más vulnerables en el acceso a agua para riego y el uso eficiente del recurso hídrico como respuesta al déficit hídrico, a través de la implementación de sistemas de riego menor y el fortalecimiento de la gestión y organización, para contribuir a la seguridad alimentaria. ii) Contribuir a asegurar la disponibilidad de agua para la conservación y recuperación de cuencas, a través de proyectos de manejo integral de cuencas (forestación, manejo de praderas nativas, vigiñas de infiltración, etc.) en cuencas con alta demanda hídrica y con riesgos de escasez hídrica, iii) Proteger las áreas productivas vulnerables a través de proyectos de gestión de riesgos (barreras vivas acompañadas de obras de encauzamiento, muros de hormigón ciclópeo y hormigón, diques longitudinales, etc.) que regulen, conduzcan y minimicen los impactos producidos por las inundaciones, torrenteras y crecidas,  iv) Promover una nueva Cultura del Agua para la Vida en el área de intervención del Programa, a través de acciones de formación, capacitación y sensibilización en niños, jóvenes, productores, regantes, técnicos y profesionales de los Gobiernos Autónomos Municipales (GAM) y Gobiernos Autónomos Departamentales (GAD), y otros actores de la cuenca, que contribuya a garantizar la sostenibilidad de las inversiones, v). Fortalecer la gobernanza local para la gestión y manejo sostenible del agua en las cuencas de intervención del programa, a través de la planificación hídrica estratégica y la elaboración de estudios de inversión que den respuesta a las demandas y necesidades en las cuencas.

2. El Ministerio de Producción Sostenible, Medio Ambiente y Agua, a través de la Unidad de Coordinación del Programa Piloto de Resiliencia Climática (UCP – PPCR), le invita a presentar Expresión de Interés para el servicio de consultoría (en adelante, los “Servicios”), para la ejecución del FORTALECIMIENTO ORGANIZACIONAL Y ASISTENCIA TÉCNICA PRODUCTIVA (FORATP) PAQUETE 2: “CONSTRUCCIÓN SISTEMA DE MICRORIEGO ALTA TICANOMA (SACACA) y MEJORAMIENTO SISTEMA DE RIEGO TECNIFICADO HUALLCA (SANTIAGO DE HUARI)”

4. El Ministerio de Producción Sostenible, Medio Ambiente y Agua, a través de la Unidad de Coordinación del Programa Piloto de Resiliencia Climática (UCP – PPCR), invita a las firmas consultoras elegibles e interesadas (en delante "Consultores") a manifestar su interés en proporcionar los Servicios. Los Consultores interesados deben proporcionar información que demuestre que tienen las calificaciones requeridas y la experiencia relevante para prestar los Servicios.

5. En el caso de firmas que tengan la intención de conformar una APCA (Asociaciones en Participación Asociación en Participación, Consorcio o Asociación), deberán presentar su carta de intención de conformación que indique los porcentajes de participación de cada firma asociada e identifique a la firma líder.

  1. Fotocopia NIT y SEPREC o documento equivalente para consultoras extranjeras
  2. Identificación de la Firma (a ser presentado en el Formulario (DOC-1).
  3. Experiencia específica: acreditar experiencia de los últimos 10 años, de los cuales deberá contar con un mínimo de 3 (tres) contratos similares relacionados con la consultoría (*). Cada contrato debe haberse realizado por un plazo igual o mayor a 6 meses, los cuales deberán estar declarados en el Formulario DOC-2, adjuntando fotocopias simples que respalden los servicios de consultoría declarados.

3.2 Servicios de Acompañamiento y/o Asistencia técnica de proyectos de Riego y/o cuenca

(**) Según la tipología de proyecto de la presente expresión de interés, se valorará preferentemente la experiencia de las mismas características.

7. Las Firmas Consultoras interesadas deberán adjuntar a su manifestación a Expresión de Interés, los Formularios DOC-1 y DOC-2 debidamente completado, así como la documentación de respaldo presentada en la Expresión de Interés.

3. Eligibility Requirement for the Assignment

The Ministry of Roads and Highways (MRH), acting through the Department of Feeder Roads, now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

(a) Minimum Mandatory Requirements (pass/fail):

  1. Core business in providing consulting services for road infrastructure projects, including design, supervision, and performance-based maintenance management.
  2. Minimum of ten (10) years of continuous business in providing consulting services for road infrastructure projects, including design, supervision, and maintenance management.
  3. Evidence of experience in at least three (3) road infrastructure consulting assignments of similar scope and complexity (design/design review and construction supervision) completed within the last ten (10) years.
  4. Evidence of experience in at least one (1) road infrastructure consulting assignment of similar scope and complexity (performance-based maintenance management) completed within the last ten (10) years.

(b) Desirable qualifications and experience (added advantages):

- Experience working in Sub-Saharan Africa, given the specific geographical, climatic, and social contexts.

- Experience with World Bank-funded or other multilateral/bilateral development bank-funded projects.

 

 Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, the Seventh (7th) Edition, September 2025 (“the Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. The Joint Venture/Sub-consultancy agreement or letter of intent to form a joint venture/a sub-consultancy association signed by every participating member shall be submitted with the Expression of Interest (EOI).

El Gobierno de la República de Honduras ha recibido financiamiento del Banco Mundial para el Proyecto de Conectividad Sostenible de Honduras y se propone utilizar una parte de los fondos para los contratos de servicios de consultoría.

Los servicios de consultoría (“los servicios”) que se pretenden contratar son: un consultor individual como Consultor COORDINADOR GENERAL DE LA UNIDAD EJECUTORA DEL PROYECTO (UEP), Los Términos de Referencia de esta asignación se encuentran publicados en la página web mencionada al final de esta solicitud, o podrán ser solicitados al Contratante a la dirección allí mencionada.

La Secretaría de Infraestructura y Transporte (SIT), invita a consultores individuales elegibles a expresar su interés en prestar los servicios solicitados. Los consultores interesados deberán proporcionar información que indique que están cualificados para suministrar los servicios. Los criterios a evaluar para la selección son:

 PERFIL DEL CONSULTOR

Experiencia

1.  Profesional Universitario con grado de licenciatura en Ingeniería Civil.

2.  Maestría o cursos de especialización en Administración de Proyectos, Gestión de Proyectos, Finanzas, Gestión de Calidad o similares.

3.  Experiencia general de quince (15) años en el ejercicio de su profesión contadas a partir de la obtención de su título a nivel universitario.

4.  Experiencia mínima de diez (10) años en cargos de Gerente, Coordinador, Director o equivalente, de Componentes o Unidades administradoras, Firmas de Supervisión o Empresas Constructoras gestionando proyectos de infraestructura.

5.  Trayectoria comprobada en la gestión de al menos dos proyectos financiados por bancos multilaterales de desarrollo o donantes internacionales.

6.  Experiencia durante los últimos 10 años, desempeñando funciones de dirección en la Supervisión, ejecución como Contratista o Coordinación del Propietario en al menos tres (3) proyectos ejecutados de rehabilitación, construcción o mejoramiento de infraestructura vial pavimentada con montos de inversión superior a 20 millones de dólares por proyecto.

 

Habilidades y Competencias

  1. Sólidas habilidades de gestión de proyectos, incluida la planificación, presupuestación, monitoreo y evaluación.
  2. Excelentes habilidades analíticas y de resolución de problemas, con atención al detalle y capacidad para gestionar asignaciones complejas.
  3. Dominio del paquete Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) y software de gestión de proyectos.
  4. Habilidades efectivas de comunicación oral y escrita en español; se valorará el dominio del inglés.
  5. Capacidad para preparar informes técnicos y de avance de alta calidad.
  6. Sólidas habilidades interpersonales y capacidad demostrada para trabajar de manera colaborativa con diversos actores, incluidas agencias gubernamentales, comunidades locales y socios internacionales.
  7. Capacidad para trabajar bajo presión y cumplir plazos ajustados.
  8. Compromiso con estándares éticos, transparencia y rendición de cuentas en la gestión de proyectos.

 

Las personas interesadas deberán detallar claramente en su hoja de vida su experiencia profesional y perfil académico, incluyendo el detalle de las funciones realizadas.

La expresión de interés de los consultores interesados, es requerida bajo el párrafo 7.34 de las Regulaciones de Adquisiciones para Prestatarios en Proyectos de Inversión publicadas por el Banco Mundial septiembre 2023, que pueden encontrarse en el sitio web www.worldbank.org. Los Consultores serán seleccionados en base al método Selección Abierta y Competitiva de Consultores Individuales descrito en las Regulaciones antes mencionada. LIBERIA REVENUE AUTHORITY

GOVERNANCE REFORM AND ACCOUNTABILITY TRANSFORMATION (GREAT) PROJECT (P177478)

IDA CREDIT No: 7511-LR

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRM SELECTION)

LR-LRA-568564-CS-CQS

Consultancy to Conduct Baseline, Midline, Endline and Post Launch VAT Awareness and Readiness Surveys

           

The Government of Liberia, through the Ministry of Finance and Development Planning (MFDP), is implementing the Governance Reform and Accountability Transformation (GREAT) Project with financing from the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank. The Project supports reforms aimed at strengthening domestic revenue mobilization, public financial management, accountability, and institutional capacity.

Under Component 2 of the Project, support is being provided to strengthen domestic revenue mobilization, including capacity building for the implementation of Value Added Tax (VAT). The Government of Liberia is transitioning from the Goods and Services Tax (GST) to VAT, which is scheduled to take effect on January 1, 2027. To support the transition, the GREAT Project is financing a nationwide VAT implementation and awareness program to be implemented by the Liberia Revenue Authority (LRA) and MFDP.

The VAT implementation program seeks to achieve at least 70 percent taxpayer awareness of VAT obligations and at least 70 percent business readiness to comply by December 2026. To independently measure progress against these results, the GREAT Project intends to engage a qualified consulting firm to conduct a series of baseline, midline, endline and post-launch VAT awareness and readiness surveys.

SCOPE OF THE ASSIGNMENT

The consulting services will include the design, implementation, analysis and reporting of four survey rounds covering VAT awareness and business readiness. The assignment will include:

  • A nationwide Baseline VAT Awareness and Readiness Survey covering approximately 1,500 respondents across Liberia's fifteen counties;
  • A Midline VAT Awareness and Readiness Survey covering approximately 800 respondents;
  • A nationwide Endline VAT Awareness and Readiness Survey covering approximately 1,500 respondents; and
  • A Post-Launch VAT Survey and Outcome Assessment covering approximately 1,000 respondents.

The consulting firm will be responsible for, among other activities, developing the survey methodology and sampling strategy; developing and piloting survey instruments; undertaking field data collection; implementing quality assurance procedures; cleaning, validating and analyzing survey data; measuring changes in taxpayer awareness and business readiness across survey rounds; assessing the reach and effectiveness of the VAT awareness campaign; and preparing the required survey reports, datasets, codebooks and analytical documentation.

The four survey rounds will be undertaken under a single consultancy assignment to ensure consistency in the survey methodology, core instruments, sampling approach, indicator definitions and analytical framework and to enable reliable comparison of results over time.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment provides further information on the scope of services and deliverables.

REQUIRED CONSULTING FIRM'S QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE

The Liberia Revenue Authority, through the GREAT Project, now invites the consulting firms receiving this Request for Expressions of Interest to indicate their interest in providing the services.

Interested consulting firms should provide information demonstrating that they possess the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the assignment. At a minimum, the consulting firm should demonstrate:

  1. At least five (5) years of demonstrated experience in survey research, socioeconomic research, market or public opinion research, monitoring and evaluation, or related applied research;
  2. Successful completion of at least three (3) similar survey assignments within the last five (5) years, involving large-scale quantitative data collection and analysis, of which at least one assignment involved nationwide or multi-county/multi-region coverage;
  3. Demonstrated experience in designing and implementing surveys involving businesses, taxpayers, households or the general public, including development of sampling methodologies, survey instruments, field protocols and analytical frameworks;
  4. Demonstrated experience conducting baseline, follow-up, perception, awareness, knowledge, attitude, readiness or comparable surveys designed to measure changes in indicators or outcomes over time;
  5. Demonstrated experience managing large-scale field data collection, including recruitment and training of enumerators, multi-location deployment, field supervision and implementation of data quality assurance procedures;
  6. Demonstrated experience with computer-assisted data collection, survey data management, statistical analysis, weighting and preparation of analytical reports;
  7. Demonstrated experience conducting surveys in Liberia or comparable West African contexts, including the capacity to mobilize field teams and undertake data collection across geographically dispersed locations; and
  8. Experience undertaking research related to taxation, domestic revenue mobilization, regulatory compliance, business formalization, public-sector reform or public awareness/behavior-change programs will be considered an advantage.

Relevant assignments should be presented in a table indicating, at a minimum, the name of the assignment, brief description/scope of services, client, country/location, contract start and completion dates, and client contact/reference information. Supporting documentation demonstrating successful completion of the assignments may be requested.

KEY EXPERTS

The consulting firm will be required to provide a minimum of eight (8) person-months of professional input through the following three key experts:

  • KE-1: Survey Specialist/Team Leader – 3 person-months
  • KE-2: Sampling Statistician/Data Analyst – 2 person-months
  • KE-3: Data Management and Field Operations Specialist – 3 person-months

At the Expression of Interest stage, firms should demonstrate their ability to mobilize suitably qualified experts for the assignment. Detailed qualification and experience requirements for each key expert are provided in the Terms of Reference.

EVALUATION OF EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

Expressions of Interest will be evaluated based on the following criteria:

Evaluation Criterion

Weight

General qualifications of the consulting firm relevant to the assignment

25%

Relevant experience in similar assignments

70%

Availability of the required key experts

5%

Total

100%

The minimum qualifying score is 70 percent.

The consulting firm ranked first based on the evaluation of Expressions of Interest will be invited to submit its technical and financial proposal for the assignment in accordance with the Consultants' Qualifications Selection (CQS) procedure.

DURATION OF THE ASSIGNMENT

The consultancy is expected to be implemented over a period of approximately Seventy Working Days. The services will be undertaken on an intermittent basis in accordance with the timing of the baseline, midline, endline and post-launch survey rounds and the associated reporting requirements.

SELECTION METHOD

The consulting firm will be selected using the Consultants' Qualifications Selection (CQS) method under a Limited Competition approach, in accordance with the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, September 2025.

This Request for Expressions of Interest is therefore being issued directly to a limited number of qualified consulting firms identified as having relevant experience and capacity to undertake the assignment.

Consulting firms may associate with other firms in the form permitted under the applicable World Bank Procurement Regulations to enhance their qualifications. The attention of interested consulting firms is drawn to the applicable provisions of the World Bank Procurement Regulations concerning eligibility and conflict of interest.

SUBMISSION OF EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

Expressions of Interest should provide sufficient information demonstrating the firm's qualifications and relevant experience to undertake the assignment. Firms are not required to submit a full technical or financial proposal at this stage.

Expressions of Interest must be submitted in both hard copy and soft copy on a USB drive in a format that cannot be altered (PDF format is preferred) to the address below by Friday, September 11, 2026, at 16:00 GMT and clearly indicate:

As a team member of the Project Management Unit (PMU), Senior Dam Specialist shall provide senior-level technical leadership, independent review, and quality assurance for the feasibility confirmation, detailed design, and implementation readiness of KV WaSIP – Sisneri Water Supply Project, with a focus on ensuring that the proposed dam, reservoir, intake, source augmentation works, and associated bulk water supply infrastructure are technically sound, safe, climate-resilient, operable, constructible, and fit for long-term service.
