Selection Method

CQS

 

The Federated States of Micronesia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Pacific Islands Regional Oceanscape Program - Second Phase for Economic Resilience (PROPER), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services are for the assessment of existing coastal fisheries data systems and gaps and the design of a recommended coastal fisheries data management framework for future implementation. The assignment will cover the four FSM States of Yap, Chuuk, Pohnpei, and Kosrae and is expected to take approximately 12 months.

The FSM Department of Resources & Development (DRD), in collaboration with State Fisheries Departments, NORMA , now invites eligible consulting firms to indicate their interest in providing the Services.

1. Objective and Scope of the Assignment

The objective of the consultancy is to assess existing coastal fisheries data systems and gaps, and to design a recommended data management framework for future implementation. The following areas are not within the scope of the assignment: 1) training, 2) conduct ecological field surveys, 3) build databases, 4) validate protocols, or and 5) produce management recommendations. These activities are intended to be undertaken under subsequent consultancies.

Stage

Main Activity

Expected Output / Focus

1

Desk Review and Data Inventory

Existing literature, research reports, available databases, catch and effort, landings, market, ecological data, and metadata catalogue.

2

Stakeholder Engagement

Fact-finding and prioritization with State fisheries departments, research institutions, and communities; information disaggregated by gender, age group, and fishing role where feasible.

3

Data Quality and Gap Assessment

Gap analysis and scoring matrix covering completeness, accuracy, timeliness, consistency, accessibility, and dataset quality tiers.

4

Institutional Assessment

Review of data-related capacity, systems, workflows, reporting, responsibilities, and data-sharing mechanisms.

5

Recommended Data Collection Protocols

Recommended SOPs for catch, effort, market, and biological data collection aligned with SPC, WCPFC, and FAO ASFIS references.

6

Data Storage, Access, and Governance Framework

Recommended database architecture, hosting, backup, user permissions, ownership, interoperability, sustainability, and accessibility arrangements.

7

State-Specific Ecological Assessment TORs

Four separate procurement-ready TORs for Yap, Chuuk, Pohnpei, and Kosrae, based on data assessment outcomes.

8

Ecological Assessment Data Needs Prioritization

Prioritized sequence of future State ecological data collection assessments, including maps and GIS coordinates of priority sites.

9

Data Management Implementation Roadmap

Phased implementation roadmap with estimated costs, sequencing, and dependencies.

10

Other Subsequent Consultancy TORs

Procurement-ready TORs for data training and mentoring, protocol validation, database build-out/deployment, and data entry mobile applications.

11

Final Report and Presentation

Final consultancy report, handover package, and presentation of findings.

3. Required Firm Experience and Shortlisting Criteria

Interested consulting firms should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. Expressions of Interest should focus on firm-level qualifications and relevant experience. Key Experts will not be evaluated at this shortlisting stage.

Criterion

Indicative considerations

Suggested evidence

Relevant fisheries data management experience

Experience assessing and designing fisheries data systems, metadata catalogues, data quality frameworks, data gap assessments, and data governance arrangements.

Project descriptions, client references, outputs, dates, countries, and contract values.

Coastal fisheries and Pacific/small island context

Experience in coastal fisheries, community fisheries, ecological information needs, and Pacific Island or small island developing state contexts. FSM experience is preferred.

Examples of comparable assignments in Pacific Island countries or similar contexts.

Institutional and capacity assessment experience

Experience reviewing institutional workflows, data-sharing mechanisms, reporting responsibilities, and data-related capacity needs for public agencies.

Institutional assessment reports or project summaries.

Data standards and interoperability

Experience applying fisheries data standards, metadata, QA/QC, and relevant standards or references such as SPC coastal fisheries minimum datasets, WCPFC standards, FAO ASFIS codes, and other recognized ecological data methods.

GIS and spatial prioritization

TOR and implementation roadmap preparation

Experience preparing procurement-ready TORs, implementation roadmaps, costed action plans, and phased system implementation recommendations.

The firm should demonstrate that it can mobilize a qualified team. The TOR identifies the following indicative key personnel:

Description

  • Description of any proposed association, joint venture, or sub-consultancy arrangement;

Prior to implementation investments, FSM requires an assessment of existing datasets, information systems, institutional arrangements, and data/ecological information gaps. The FSM Coastal Fisheries SAR 2023 is the foundational reference for identifying priority data and ecological assessment needs across Yap, Chuuk, Pohnpei, and Kosrae.

The assignment will produce a data inventory and metadata catalogue, data quality and gap assessment with scoring matrix, institutional capacity assessment focused on data-related capacity, recommended standardized data collection protocols, recommended data storage/access/governance framework, ecological assessment data needs prioritization, four State-specific ecological data collection TORs, a phased data management implementation roadmap, and procurement-ready TORs for subsequent implementation consultancies.

The assignment is assessment and design focused. It excludes implementation training, ecological field surveys, database build-out, protocol validation, mobile application rollout, and management recommendations

The GP intends to apply part of the proceeds of this loan for eligible payments for the consultancy services to be procured under the project.

The consulting services comprise the development of a website for the Green Plan.

 

2. Objective of the assignment

The objective of this assignment is to design, develop, and deploy a secure, scalable, and user-friendly website that:

® Promotes Green Plan programs and activities and Gate Project activities

® Serves as the official communication platform for the Green Plan, including the webpage development of GATE Project;

® Ensures public access to project information, progress reports, …

® Enhances stakeholder engagement and communication by providing access to project information, updates, and communication channels.

® Facilitates grievance management by enabling stakeholders to submit grievances through a dedicated Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM);

® Enables efficient internal content management by non-technical staff.

 

3. Scope of Services

The Consultant shall provide all services required for the successful implementation of the assignment, including but not limited to: requirements analysis, system design, UX/UI design, prototyping, system development, CMS implementation, configuration of functional modules, integration of dashboards, GIS and external systems, testing and quality assurance, deployment and go-live support, training and capacity building, warranty, maintenance, technical support, and preparation of all documentation and handover materials required for final acceptance.

The assignment shall be implemented in the following phases:

- Phase I: Requirements Analysis and System Design

- Phase II: System Development and Configuration

- Phase III: Testing, Deployment, and Go-Live

- Phase V: Warranty, Maintenance, and Technical Support

These phases describe the implementation sequence only and shall not be interpreted as payment milestones.

The Green Plan now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Consultant brochures may also be included in the Expression of Interest (EOI).

 

5. Evaluation Criteria

Expressions of Interest will be evaluated using a 100-point scoring system based on the following criteria and weights:

Criterion 1: General experience of the firm (30/100)

This criterion assesses the firm’s overall experience and track record, including years of relevant experience and the number and type of websites successfully delivered.  Criterion 2: Experience in Similar Assignments within the last 10 years (25/100)

This criterion assesses the firm's experience in successfully delivering assignments of similar nature, scope and complexity to the required services. Similar assignments may include, but are not limited to, website design and development, CMS implementation and customization, online forms, interactive website functionalities, and website maintenance and technical support.

The Firm shall provide details of its own similar contracts, including, for each reference project, the client's name, project title, a brief description of the services provided, website URL(s) (where applicable), CMS/platform used, completion date, and contract value.

The proposed scoring under this criterion would be:

- Minimum 7 years of professional experience in website design, development, and implementation.

- Minimum 5 years of professional experience in managing and delivering similar website development assignments, including CMS-based and multilingual websites.

2. Website Designer (Key Expert) (10/25)

- University degree or equivalent qualification in Web Design, Graphic Design, Computer Science, or a related field.

- Minimum 7 years of professional experience in designing user-friendly and responsive websites.

- Minimum 5 years of professional experience in designing modern website interfaces, including multilingual and mobile-friendly websites.

Alternatively, the REOI evaluation could remain limited to the consulting firm's experience and capacity, with information on available technical resources provided only for reference, as currently reflected in the REOI.

Criterion 4: Experience with Government Institutions, Donor-Funded Projects and NGOs within the last 10 years (20/100)

This criterion assesses the firm's experience in providing similar services to government institutions, donor-funded projects, international organizations, and non-governmental organizations (NGOs). It evaluates the firm's familiarity with the working environment, requirements and standards typically associated with such organizations.

The firm shall provide relevant portfolios and supporting documents to substantiate the information provided under the above evaluation criteria. Such documents may include, where applicable, website links, project references, completion certificates, client references, or other evidence demonstrating the Applicant’s experience and qualifications.

The Expression of Interest should not exceed 50 pages.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.13, 3.15, and 3.16 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” (February 2025), which set forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

 

 

Country:  MOZAMBIQUE

Project:  Mphanda Nkuwa Hydroelectric Project

Agreement: Preparation Advance No. -V522-MZ.

Assignment Title: Individual Consultancy Services to Provision Hydrologist Specialist Project Advisor for providing Project Advisory to undertaking the review of the hydrological studies of the planned Mphanda Nkuwa Hydropower Project.

 

Reference: MZ-GMNK-442364-CS-INDV

 

 

 

The Government of Mozambique (GoM) hereinafter referred to as “the Borrower” have received Advance funds from International Development Association (IDA) towards the costs of the Mphanda Nkuwa Hydroelectric Project, Preparation Phase. The funds have been channeled through the Mphanda Nkuwa Hydroelectric Project Office (GMNK) as the Project Implementation Agency, and GMNK intends to apply part of the proceeds for Consulting Services for providing Project Advisory for undertaking the review of the hydrological studies of the planned Mphanda Nkuwa Hydropower Project.

 

 

The GMNK now invites eligible Individual Consultant (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the Services. Interested Individual Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services. The shortlisting criteria are:

 

  1. qualification, experience and skills in providing Project advisory services for reviewing the hydrological studies of hydropower projects;
  2. a minimum of Post Graduate Degree in the relevant hydrological disciplines and must have at least 15 years of professional experience relevant to the assignment.
  3. description of similar assignments previously carried out - must have done at least two (2) similar assignments (hydrological of hydropower advisory services), and
  4. experience of working in Sub-Sahara Africa - at least one (1) of the assignments should be in Sub-Shara Africa - and other regions.

 

Evidence shall be attached as supporting documents for the Expression of Interest.

 

Objective

 

The Project is being prepared for seeking financial support of the World Bank (the “Bank”) and therefore must comply with the World Bank Safeguards Policies and Performance Standards (see the concept project information document stage at the WB website [1]).  Accordingly, the Mphanda Nkuwa Project needs to comply with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) – Community Health and Safety (ESS4[2]). To this effect two panel of experts (PoEs) need to be formed: (i) Panel of Experts for Dam Safety (PoE-DS); and (ii) Panel of Experts for Environmental and Social Management (PoE-ESM).

Key Responsibilities/ Scope of Reviews

 

The hydrologist will:

 

  1. Review of the hydrological studies pertaining to the long-term inflow to the reservoirs, and spillway and diversion design floods with reference to international criteria. Assess the adequacy of spillway and diversion facilities, also considering increasing hydrological variability associated with global warming. Review of soil erosion data and estimate of sediment yield into the reservoirs, estimated reservoir sedimentation, and assessment of the long-term sustainable capacity that could be maintained by implementing appropriate management strategies. Review of layouts related to sediment management of the reservoirs including sediment flushing.
  2. Review of the design of spillway and tailrace facilities including flow conditions, energy dissipation and need for hydraulic modelling.
  3. Review of the designs of the diversion works, schedule and risk factors associated with diversion during construction and with the closure of diversion works at initial reservoir filling.

 

Expected Assignment Timeline

 

The assignment is for a period of six (6) years, covering project preparation, construction, and initial reservoir filling. The initial contract will be signed for a period of 2 years, with the potential for an extension to cover the full duration of preparation and implementation. The contract will be time-based, with an annual ceiling of 20 working days, subject to extension if needed.

 

Detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the address given below.
